(Photo by PETER POWELL / AFP) After a slow start, a fiery-tempered encounter sparked into life when Everton midfielder Harrison Armstrong launched into a tackle on Josh Acheampong for the first of five first-half yellow cards. ‘More Flair’ That challenge also enlivened the home crowd and spurred Everton on to their best spell of the game. Thierno Barry was guilty of another wasteful day in front of goal as the Frenchman planted a header from Jack Grealish’s cross too close to Martinez. Chelsea have made a habit of fast starts under Alonso, but it took until four minutes before half-time to threaten when Moises Caicedo blasted off the bar from a well-worked corner. Everton were furious that Morgan Rogers escaped a second booking just before the break after a thunderous clash with England teammate James Garner. That proved to be a huge decision as the visitors this time flew out of the blocks at the start of the second period. Jorrel Hato got to the byline and his low cross fell to Neto, who had time to control before firing low past Jordan Pickford. Chelsea had not kept a Premier League clean sheet since January, but were rarely troubled by an Everton side short on forward options despite the loss of Martinez. “I just felt that Chelsea had that little bit more flair and ability which we didn’t possess at the right moments today,” said Everton boss David Moyes. The treatment for Martinez threatened to halt Chelsea’s momentum as they controlled the second half. Belgian Mike Penders replaced the Chelsea number one for his first Premier League appearance but had little to do bar dealing with a few desperate Everton crosses. At the other end, Pickford made a fine save to deny Joao Pedro. But Chelsea did get their second goal when Neto coolly stroked it into the bottom corner after Jordan Henderson’s free-kick was blocked by the Everton wall. item.title: 3 Things to Watch in Chargers-Chiefs: Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston are good to go in Week 6
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Defensive co-ordinator Chris O'Leary and inside linebacker coach Sean Spence of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrate a stop of the Los Angeles Rams on fourth and goal during the first half in a preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Chargers-Chiefs this week and as much as I’d like to be able to say this one is for sole possession of first place in the AFC West, I cannot. One team is winless and the other is undefeated. This one does not look good on paper. By records alone, it also doesn’t look like a fun watch for anyone that isn’t already a fan of either team. But hey, it’s a divisional matchup that has given us plenty of entertaining watches over the last decade. More than likely this one will still do the same. That said, here are three things I’ll be watching closely when these teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) What will the offense look like just one week before the bye? There’s a very strong chance the Chargers simply play it safe with their numerous injuries and use this week as one more opportunity to see what the bottom of the roster has within them. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, and Brenen Thompson are all hobbled and have been limited through the first two practices this week. Tre’ Harris is in even worse shape as he has been a DNP thus far. KeAndre Lambert-Smith just had his 21-day window activated and it looks like he’s trending to return this week. That development may lead the Chargers to take a cautious approach with their top guys just one week from the bye. Let’s just be honest, the offense honestly looks no better no matter who is out there unless it’s a healthy McConkey. He hasn’t been healthy since Week One and it’s about time we let him get to 100 percent before he steps back out on the field. Right now, Justin Herbert’s healthy receivers are Theo Wease, Derius Davis, and Marquez Valdez-Scantling. On the practice squad, they have Gary Jennings and the recently-signed Luke Grimm. Jennings is out of game day elevations which means he’d have to be signed to the active roster in order to participate against the Chiefs. With Alec Ingold now on IR, Jennings could take that spot if the team chooses. As for the offensive line, will they send out four rookies for another week? Will veteran Daniel Brunskill learn the offense enough to start at right tackle for Alex Harkey? We’ll have to see come game day. UPDATE: Both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were removed from the final injury report meaning Justin Herbert will have his two top wideouts back this Sunday. 2.) Will Omarion Hampton continue to see his snaps share decrease? Hampton played only 31.7 percent of the offense’s snaps against the Broncos, although he did receive over 40 percent of the running back carries. With each week, Hampton is playing less and less. item.content:encoded: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Defensive co-ordinator Chris O'Leary and inside linebacker coach Sean Spence of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrate a stop of the Los Angeles Rams on fourth and goal during the first half in a preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Chargers-Chiefs this week and as much as I’d like to be able to say this one is for sole possession of first place in the AFC West, I cannot. One team is winless and the other is undefeated. This one does not look good on paper. By records alone, it also doesn’t look like a fun watch for anyone that isn’t already a fan of either team. But hey, it’s a divisional matchup that has given us plenty of entertaining watches over the last decade. More than likely this one will still do the same. That said, here are three things I’ll be watching closely when these teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) What will the offense look like just one week before the bye? There’s a very strong chance the Chargers simply play it safe with their numerous injuries and use this week as one more opportunity to see what the bottom of the roster has within them. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, and Brenen Thompson are all hobbled and have been limited through the first two practices this week. Tre’ Harris is in even worse shape as he has been a DNP thus far. KeAndre Lambert-Smith just had his 21-day window activated and it looks like he’s trending to return this week. That development may lead the Chargers to take a cautious approach with their top guys just one week from the bye. Let’s just be honest, the offense honestly looks no better no matter who is out there unless it’s a healthy McConkey. He hasn’t been healthy since Week One and it’s about time we let him get to 100 percent before he steps back out on the field. Right now, Justin Herbert’s healthy receivers are Theo Wease, Derius Davis, and Marquez Valdez-Scantling. On the practice squad, they have Gary Jennings and the recently-signed Luke Grimm. Jennings is out of game day elevations which means he’d have to be signed to the active roster in order to participate against the Chiefs. With Alec Ingold now on IR, Jennings could take that spot if the team chooses. As for the offensive line, will they send out four rookies for another week? Will veteran Daniel Brunskill learn the offense enough to start at right tackle for Alex Harkey? We’ll have to see come game day. UPDATE: Both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were removed from the final injury report meaning Justin Herbert will have his two top wideouts back this Sunday. 2.) Will Omarion Hampton continue to see his snaps share decrease? Hampton played only 31.7 percent of the offense’s snaps against the Broncos, although he did receive over 40 percent of the running back carries. With each week, Hampton is playing less and less. Kimani Vidal’s huge 42-yard touchdown rumble will not do him any favors in getting back anywhere lose to workhorse duties. It also doesn’t help that Mike McDaniel continues to force Keaton Mitchell into the game plan to run sweeps to specifically the right side. Defenses know what’s coming when either back is in, which can’t be good for a Chargers offense that already isn’t fooling anyone in anyway. The Chiefs have a great defense. Their linebackers can fly, hit hard, and blitz. Chris Jones is still a menace along the interior and George Karlaftis is an ascending pass rusher. They’re about to face a very young Chargers offensive line and it may not even matter which running back is in. Hampton, in my opinion, is still the Chargers’ most talented back. I don’t think he’s a timeshare guy and his ability to punish deep into the fourth quarter was an aid to the Bolts last season as they closed out games with the ball in their hands. It’d be nice to get back to that kind of football. But seeing how things are going, we may never see that again (at least, maybe until next year?). 3.) Can Chris O’Leary’s defense continue their strong start against another elite offense? After a rough outing in Week One against the Cardinals, O’Leary’s unit has been one of the best in the entire league the past four weeks. Check out these numbers: Chris O’Leary’s #Chargers defense over the last 4 games: – 5th in EPA/play – 7th in success rate – 5th in dropback/EPA – 11th in EPA/rush – 6th in dropback success rate – 14th in rushing success rate pic.twitter.com/agcgGawueE — Guilty As Charged Podcast (@GACPodcast17) October 12, 2026 Despite not having Derwin James and Donte Jackson in their past two games, they’re still a top-1o unit in EPA/play, success rate, and dropback/EPA. The efficiency is insane for a group that’s far and away the leader in most drives started within their own territory (18!). Compared to the Saints who are second with 11, that’s even more unreal. They got Josh Allen and the Bills to turn the ball over five times and helped put a lid on both Sam Darnold and Bo Nix the past two weeks. Now they will face Patrick Mahomes and the revitalized Chiefs offense that now features Kenneth Walker and a highly-productive rushing attack. O’Leary doesn’t need the team to win this game for it to be a personal “W” in his book. If the defense does their part, records a turnover or two, and helps keep this one close, no one will be able to say another word about his group not pulling their weight.

item.title: ‘We’ve Let Our Fans Down’ — Titans CEO Makes Feelings Clear on Tennessee’s 0–5 Start, Robert Saleh’s Future As HC
item.description: ‘We’ve Let Our Fans Down’ — Titans CEO Makes Feelings Clear on Tennessee’s 0–5 Start, Robert Saleh’s Future As HC The Tennessee Titans are among the three NFL teams still searching for their first victory of the season. Robert Saleh’s first season as head coach has undoubtedly become a frustrating experience for fans. However, Titans CEO Burke Nihill understands the frustration and anger among the fan base while continuing to express his support for head coach Robert Saleh and general manager Mike Borgonzi. Titans CEO Addresses Fans’ Anger After Tennessee’s Disastrous Start The Titans’ offensive struggles have been a major factor behind their winless start. Tennessee ranks last in PFN’s NFL Offense Impact rankings, earning a grade of just 67.9. The team’s latest loss once again exposed their offensive struggles. Tennessee suffered a disappointing 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans in Week 5, managing just 187 total yards. During an interview with ESPN on Friday, Nihill addressed fans’ disappointment and accepted responsibility for the team’s inability to deliver better results. “The first thing I would say back to the fans is just that we’re sorry,” Nihill said . “There’s nobody in this building that doesn’t feel a sense of grief about it, because not only are we fans of the team as well, but we feel the sense of responsibility to deliver. And we’ve let our fans down because football is supposed to be fun.” BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator The franchise is coming off two consecutive 3-14 seasons. Now, the latest defeat dropped the Titans to fourth place in the AFC South with a 0-5 record. However, when a team opens a season with five consecutive losses, questions about the head coach’s future become difficult to avoid. Those concerns are particularly significant in Tennessee, where the franchise fired at least one coach or general manager in each calendar year from 2022 through 2025. Despite the pressure surrounding the team’s winless start, Nihill remains confident in Saleh and Borgonzi. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer “I believe that Mike Borgonzi and Robert Saleh are ultimately going to get this team out of the woods and restore it to competitive football,” he said. “The train is on the tracks. It just hasn’t picked up momentum, but it will.” The Titans CEO added, “I can confidently say this organization is in a place where there is organizational belief in Mike, in Robert, and they absolutely have all the support they need to get this train moving and moving faster.” The Titans’ supporters are waiting for more than an apology. They want to see progress, and, above all, their first win of the 2026 NFL season. Tennessee will now turn its attention to its upcoming matchup against the Indianapolis Colts, hoping to end its losing streak and finally give its frustrated fan base something to celebrate. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Timberwolves get major reality check despite LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards pairing from former head coach
item.description: © Sam Sharpe-Imagn Images Timberwolves get major reality check despite LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards pairing from former head coach appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Minnesota Timberwolves enter the 2026-27 NBA season with one of the league’s most intriguing backcourts following the acquisition of LaMelo Ball to pair with Anthony Edwards. However, former NBA head coach Tyrone Corbin believes Minnesota’s championship aspirations will ultimately depend on its defense rather than its offensive firepower. Speaking with Kyle Odegard of NEXTPredict, Corbin expressed confidence in Ball and Edwards developing chemistry but questioned whether the Timberwolves can consistently slow opposing teams. “They’re going to have to get some stops at some point. Offensively, you look at the talent they’ll have on the floor in those two guys alone, they’re going to be able to score the ball. Do they have enough to figure out how to slow other teams?” Corbin said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “There are some nights you just can’t force your will on a team, and defense will save you. With Rudy Gobert anchoring in there I hope it will help some, but they’re going to need to stay in front of their guys at some point.” Minnesota finished its preseason with a 3-3 record, including a 133-116 loss to the Chicago Bulls on Friday night. Despite his defensive concerns, Corbin expects Ball and Edwards to complement each other offensively. “Easy. They both are dynamic offensive talents. LaMelo can score from anywhere but he can really pass the ball. You have to make sure the guys on the floor with him are looking, because he will throw it from anywhere and get it there.” Tyrone Corbin believes LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards can thrive together Ball’s arrival gives Edwards another established offensive creator capable of generating scoring opportunities for himself and his teammates. Corbin also believes their personalities will help accelerate the adjustment. “He is a great, great young man. I think his personality, and the things I hear about Ant’s personality, is that they’ll mesh pretty quickly, and that talent on the floor will come together.” However, Minnesota faces considerable competition in a Western Conference featuring the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs . With Gobert anchoring the interior defense, the Timberwolves have an established rim protector. Still, Corbin emphasized that Minnesota’s perimeter defenders must provide sufficient resistance to maximize the team’s potential. “They’re going to be good, man. To have Edwards there, and then add a kid like LaMelo, and Rudy in the middle. With the way they’re going to be able to score, if they can get some stops, they’re going to be something to reckon with in the West.” The Timberwolves will begin their regular season Wednesday, Oct. 21, against Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat on the road. item.title: Analyst Lists DK Metcalf as a Trade Target for the Colts
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Michael Roberts, Editor Could DK Metcalf end up with the Indianapolis Colts? Recently, Aaron Zacharias of Horseshoe Heroes wrote about wide receivers the Colts need to consider before the NFL Trade Deadline passes. Metcalf, who’s currently with the Pittsburgh Steelers , was on the list: “DK Metcalf (Pittsburgh Steelers) DK Metcalf is the least likely on this list for the Colts’ future ambitions, but he’s also the most interesting possible target. Either it’s the Aaron Rodgers factor, or he’s simply not a good fit with the Pittsburgh Steelers; Metcalf has, in any case, not worked out. There is a world where the Steelers could trade Metcalf after just one and a half seasons, or wait until they get a different quarterback next year. That said, if there is any interest in him from other teams, would the Steelers turn it away? The Colts could land a No. 1 target with actual No. 1 target experience.” Without a doubt, Indianapolis needs help at the wide receiver position. Does trading for DK Metcalf make sense? Analyst Lists DK Metcalf as a Trade Target for the Colts The Seattle Seahawks drafted DK Metcalf in the second round (64th overall pick) of the 2019 NFL Draft. As a rookie, he caught 58 passes for 900 yards and seven touchdowns. He recorded seven receptions for 160 yards and a touchdown in Seattle’s playoff win over the Philadelphia Eagles . It was the NFL record for most receiving yards by a rookie in a postseason game. In 2020, Metcalf finished with 83 receptions for 1,303 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. He also made the Pro Bowl and was named a second-team All-Pro. Metcalf finished the 2023 campaign with 66 receptions for 1,114 yards and eight touchdowns. He was named to the second Pro Bowl of his career that year. DK Metcalf was later traded to the Steelers in 2025. During his career in Pittsburgh, he has caught 78 passes for 1,075 yards and seven touchdowns. Metcalf’s production has been underwhelming this year. In five games, he has only recorded 19 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown on 37 targets. The Last Word Sep 13, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce (14) celebrates during the first quarter against the Baltimore Ravens at Lucas Oil Stadium. Analyst Lists DK Metcalf as a Trade Target for the Colts The Seattle Seahawks drafted DK Metcalf in the second round (64th overall pick) of the 2019 NFL Draft. As a rookie, he caught 58 passes for 900 yards and seven touchdowns. He recorded seven receptions for 160 yards and a touchdown in Seattle’s playoff win over the Philadelphia Eagles . It was the NFL record for most receiving yards by a rookie in a postseason game. In 2020, Metcalf finished with 83 receptions for 1,303 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. He also made the Pro Bowl and was named a second-team All-Pro. Metcalf finished the 2023 campaign with 66 receptions for 1,114 yards and eight touchdowns. He was named to the second Pro Bowl of his career that year. DK Metcalf was later traded to the Steelers in 2025. During his career in Pittsburgh, he has caught 78 passes for 1,075 yards and seven touchdowns. Metcalf’s production has been underwhelming this year. In five games, he has only recorded 19 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown on 37 targets. The Last Word Sep 13, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce (14) celebrates during the first quarter against the Baltimore Ravens at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images The Colts wide receiver room is not elite by any stretch of the imagination. It wouldn’t be great even if Alec Pierce was available. Pierce is currently out with a heel injury, and is reportedly still a few weeks away from returning to the field. The former Cincinnati Bearcat signed a four-year, $114 million extension with the Colts during the offseason. Pierce was supposed to be “The Man” for Indy, but he has only played in two games this season. Fellow Colts receivers like Josh Downs and newcomer Keenan Allen haven’t stepped up in Pierce’s absence. The team was rumored to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr., but the Arizona Cardinals , of course, traded him to the Houston Texans instead. Should Indy trade for DK Metcalf before this year’s November 10 Trade Deadline? The Colts could use a two-time Pro Bowler like Metcalf. Yet, it’s unclear what the team would have to give up in a deal. Plus, it’s unclear whether the Steelers would even be willing to trade him. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones would surely love to add DK Metcalf. What quarterback wouldn’t want to add another offensive playmaker? Metcalf could team with tight end Tyler Warren and improve the team’s pass-catching corps. But it’s unlikely that such a trade will happen. item.title: Muheim produces late magic again as Hamburg stun Stuttgart
item.description: Muheim produces late magic again as Hamburg stun Stuttgart Despite facing their third away fixture in just seven days, Sebastian Hoeneß’s Stuttgart side started brightly in Hamburg, dominated possession early, and created several promising chances. But, it was Hamburg who posed the initial attacking threat, as Fabio Vieira intercepted a misplaced pass from Angelo Stiller in the fifth minute but failed to convert, sending his shot wide of Dennis Seimen’s goal. The visitors gradually asserted themselves, with Deniz Undav meeting a delivery from Bilal El Khannouss and directing it over the crossbar with his shoulder; shortly after, Hamburg-born Ermedin Demirovic headed another cross from the Moroccan wide in the 15th minute. Stuttgart dominated possession in the opening stages, holding over 80%, but Merlin Polzin’s side grew into the contest and nearly took the lead in the 27th minute when a corner from Miro Muheim found Sebastian Bornauw, whose header deflected off Vieira and Seimen made an impressive save. The visitors kept the pressure on and came closest to breaking the deadlock six minutes before the interval, as a well-executed counterattack let Jamie Leweling pick out Undav in the penalty area, but the Stuttgart captain’s first-time effort hit the post. Demirovic then saw a header denied by Daniel Heuer Fernandes, ensuring that both teams entered the interval goalless. Yousuff Poulsen nearly scored for the hosts three minutes into the second half, striking the post following a lofted pass from David Moller Wolfe. As in previous fixtures in Paderborn and Bratislava, Stuttgart sought to regain control early in the second half, though Hamburg had begun to gain the upper hand. Six minutes after his earlier attempt, Poulsen came closest to scoring, his shot striking the bar after a touch from VfB goalkeeper Seimen, while less than a minute earlier, Demirovic had sent a header just inches wide. As has been the theme of the season, the match became an end-to-end contest after Stuttgart's early dominance, with HSV looking increasingly threatening. They had an effort in the 58th minute when Undav attempted an acrobatic volley that Heuer Fernandes denied, as the half continued at a frenetic pace and the Volksparkstadion anticipated the opening goal. Heading into the weekend, a point would have been perfect for HSV, but they could well have sensed a missed opportunity in the second half had they not found the net. In the 88th minute, they finally punished Stuttgart, with Muheim hammering in from range and catching Seimen off guard with a ripper, his second late strike in a week after netting against Hoffenheim last time out. For Stuttgart, it is hard to argue that anything other than defeat was deserved. Once again, they surrendered control in the second half and struggled to get a grip as the pace increased. item.title: Füllkrug's second-half brace rescues draw for Bremen against Paderborn
item.description: Füllkrug's second-half brace rescues draw for Bremen against Paderborn Werder Bremen had to battle back and save parity against a clinical SC Paderborn this afternoon at the Weserstadion. Two first-half goals from the visitors made for a chorus of whistles at the interval, but Niclas Füllkrug's brace ensured a share of the spoils. Making home advantage count in the initial exchanges, it seemed near inevitable that Bremen would open the scoring as Niclas Füllkrug flashed wide. Minutes later, only Nahuel Noll stood between Marco Grüll and Chucki from reasonably gilt-edged positions. In a blink of an eye, however, Paderborn established a 2-0 lead. Grüll's mix up on the ball allowed Steffen Tigges to feed Stefano Marino. The 22-year-old driving into the right side of the box with speed before arrowing the ball into Karl Hein's top-right corner. Things got even better for Ralf Rangnick's men when Tigges himself netted on the half-hour. Bremen's rearguard were caught napping, letting a long throw bounce into the box for a routine toe-poke finish. Another Noll parry crucially kept out Arthur before the interval. Making one change at the breeak, Daniel Thioune's side halved the deficit just before the hour. A diagonal ball flicked on by Eren Dincki sat up nicely for Niclas Füllkrug to snap the ball inside the lower-left post. Suddenly the half-time boos made way for support. Mitchell Weiser's bench impact proved telling 7 minute later. His cross yielded a penalty after Laurin Curda's handball. Füllkrug stuck it away to take his season tally up to six. Paderborn also emptied the bench, bringing on Pieringer, Baack, Phillipe and Müller Bremen pushed to complete the comeback with Weiser and Arthur testing Noll from tight angles. Paderborn also had their chances to snatch it late on. Four minutes of injury time left Rayan Philippe with a shot that struck the post and bounced ensuring it stayed a draw.

Two first-half goals from the visitors made for a chorus of whistles at the interval, but Niclas Füllkrug's brace ensured a share of the spoils. Making home advantage count in the initial exchanges, it seemed near inevitable that Bremen would open the scoring as Niclas Füllkrug flashed wide. Grüll's mix up on the ball allowed Steffen Tigges to feed Stefano Marino. The 22-year-old driving into the right side of the box with speed before arrowing the ball into Karl Hein's top-right corner. item.title: Luis Enrique rolls the dice with heavily changed team against Strasbourg
item.description: Luis Enrique rolls the dice with heavily changed team against Strasbourg PSG have rotated their team heavily to take on Strasbourg in Ligue 1 this afternoon, with a largely second string on the pitch. If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. It’s become almost impossible to guess Luis Enrique’s starting XIs for Ligue 1 games. The coach loves to rotate in these domestic games, and he’s constantly keeping people guessing with his moves through the whole team. The fact that he has such good options in every position means he can vary the lineup massively without losing any strength. PSG rotate heavily for trip to Alsace Maghnes Akliouche scores his first PSG goal. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) For today’s game against Strasbourg, it was known in advance that Marquinhos wasn’t going to play. But his changes have actually gone much further than that. It’s as close to a second string as you’ll see from the coach. Of course Tuesday night’s game against Barcelona is a huge factor in his thinking. Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue, Fabian Ruiz, Vitinha, Nuno Mendes, Willian Pacho and Achraf Hakimi jointheir captain Marquinhos in missing out. That means the team has Matvey Safonov in goal, with a back four featuring Lucas Digne and Warren Zaire Emery at full back, with Ilya Zabarnyi and Lucas Hernandez at centre back. In midfield, Dro Fernandez makes his latest appearance, alongside Joao Neves. It looks like Lucas Beraldo will sit behind them. The front three has Ferran Torres leading the line, flanked by Khvicha Kvaratshelia and Maghnes Akliouche. That is a team that is still packed with world class quality, despite the rotation. In other news… Marquinhos is not in the team to face Strasbourg this afternoon as Luis Enrique continues his strict rotation policy. Maghnes Akliouche probably won’t get the start today – but that doesn’t mean his manager isn’t delighted with his progress.

item.title: Who could replace Otega Oweh on two-way contract? Here are 3 candidates
item.description: After filling out their roster, the Oklahoma City Thunder could be forced to make another move before Opening Night. Under sad circumstances, unfortunately. Otega Oweh sustained a season-ending torn Achilles tendon in the NBA preseason. Now that Oweh is out for the entire 2026-27 season, that puts the Thunder in a tough spot. Sure, you liked him enough to add him with the No. 41 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. But surely, you can't keep a two-way spot occupied by someone you know won't log minutes. If the Thunder eventually waive Oweh, who could replace him on a two-way deal? The other two guys for OKC under that same contract are Brooks Barnhizer and Josh Dix. Let's look at three candidates who could eventually take Oweh's spot on the NBA roster: Christoph Tilly This is probably the safest pick. Reading the tea leaves, it seems like the Thunder really like Tilly. He was the first player signed to an Exhibit-10 deal. And so far, he's the only one of the original four who remains on OKC's roster. The other three were waived on Friday. Tilley went undrafted out of Ohio State in the 2026 NBA draft. He was part of OKC's 2026 Summer League squad. He's a seven-footer who can handle and shoot the ball well for his size. Watch out for him as a realistic option to get a two-way spot. Dariq Whitehead By a slim margin, Whitehead remains eligible for a two-way spot. He has three years of NBA experience. The 2023 first-round pick is fighting for his basketball dream. Injuries have completely destroyed them. Recently signed by OKC, it seems like the organization likes the talent and is taking a flyer on him. Whitehead spent two seasons with the Brooklyn Nets. He was on a 10-day contract with the Memphis Grizzlies last year. Before that, he was putting up numbers on the G League's OKC Blue. So there's some history there. If you're looking for headlines, this is the way to go. Most NBA fans know who he is. Milos Uzan Sometimes, you gotta go outside of your bubble. In comes Uzan. He was one of the more decorated guys to go undrafted in the 2026 NBA draft. He should be a familiar name as he spent two collegiate seasons at Oklahoma before transferring to Houston. That's where he broke out. The Cougars have been a national title contender for the last few years. He helped with that. Right now, Uzan is on the Boston Celtics under an Exhibit-10 deal. But the Thunder can easily swoop in and sign him to a two-way spot. That'd be a cool story as a former Sooner. Plus, he's played well in the preseason. He recently had 14 points in an OT win over the Philadelphia 76ers. And Kelvin Sampson usually has his guys ready to defend at the NBA level. This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Who could replace Otega Oweh on two-way contract? Here are 3 candidates

item.description: ⚽ Updates on the Saturday afternoon football action ⚽ Live scoreboard | Tables | Top scorers | Email Simon Andy Hunter’s match report from the Hill Dickinson is here, and you can find it below. Chelsea have returned from the international break with an authority that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. A brace from Pedro Neto condemned Everton to an inaugural defeat of the season as the visitors climbed to fourth on the back of their first Premier League clean sheet since January. A head injury sustained by Emi Martínez, who was carried off on a stretcher after seven minutes of treatment, was the only concern from a mature display in the Merseyside sunshine for Alonso’s team. There were goalkeeping issues at both ends of the field with Jordan Pickford unconvincing for the second week in succession as David Moyes’ side suffered self-inflicted wounds. But Everton could have no complaints about the merits of Chelsea’s victory given their contrasting performances in the second half. Continue reading...

item.title: Why isn't Nico lamaleava playing for UCLA? Bruins QB out for season after injury
item.description: Why isn't Nico lamaleava playing for UCLA? Bruins QB out for season after injury originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 12th-ranked UCLA football team is off to an impressive start under head coach Bob Chesney. But the Bruins will have to continue without starting quarterback Nico lamaleava. The former five-star quarterback is out for the remainder of the season after suffering a knee injury in UCLA's victory over Oregon last week. The injury is a significant setback for the undefeated Bruins, who entered the week with a 5-0 record. With unprecedented postseason hopes on the line, UCLA must now adjust its offense as it prepares to face Wisconsin on Saturday. Iamaleava injured his left knee late in the second quarter against Oregon. He was tackled by Bear Alexander and Jerry Mixon while scrambling, with his leg appearing to twist during the play. UCLA's medical staff attended to the quarterback, who returned for one more play and threw an interception. However, he did not return to the field after halftime and was later seen without his uniform. Although UCLA had not officially confirmed his status earlier this week, Chesney acknowledged there was "serious concern" about the quarterback's condition. Iamaleava's absence leaves a significant gap in UCLA's offense. His ability to extend plays has helped the Bruins escape difficult situations, while his mobility forces opposing defenses to account for the passing game. This also creates opportunities for the rushing attack. He finishes the season with 982 passing yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions on 72-of-116 passing. He also recorded 144 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown. UCLA has two possible replacements for Iamaleava. Cal Poly transfer Ty Dieffenbach and Nico's younger brother, Madden lamaleava. Dieffenbach replaced the injured starter against Oregon, completing three of six passes for 43 yards and a touchdown. Chesney indicated that Dieffenbach would get an opportunity to start against Wisconsin. item.title: Arsenal star pushing for January exit after recent struggles
item.description: Arsenal star pushing for January exit after recent struggles Viktor Gyokeres and Arsenal Facing January Crossroads as Exit Talk Grows Arsenal may be heading towards one of the most awkward transfer subplots of the coming window, with Viktor Gyokeres increasingly unsettled and a January move now described as a genuine possibility. According to TeamTalk , the Sweden international is prepared to reassess his future after a rapid change in standing under Mikel Arteta. The striking part of this developing story is the speed of the shift. Gyokeres arrived from Sporting CP in 2025 amid significant expectation, after Arsenal chose him ahead of Benjamin Sesko. He then delivered in a major way, scoring 21 goals in all competitions, including 14 in the Premier League, and playing his part in a title-winning season as well as a run to the Champions League final. That return should have strengthened his place. Instead, the current picture appears very different. TeamTalk states that “Viktor Gyokeres is ready to quit Arsenal and is set to push for a January exit”, a line that underlines the seriousness of the situation. The report adds that frustration over his minutes is central, with the striker “yet to start a Premier League game this season”. Premier League starts at centre of Arsenal concern From the player’s perspective, the issue seems straightforward. A striker of Gyokeres’ profile and age does not want to drift through the first half of a season waiting for opportunities. Sources cited in the report say “his lack of opportunities is the main reason he is now looking towards the exit door”, and there is little ambiguity in that. Photo IMAGO Arsenal’s internal thinking may be more layered. Kai Havertz is “currently the preferred option”, while long-term admiration for Julian Alvarez remains active in the background. The report notes that Arsenal’s pursuit of Alvarez over the summer was “a development that could not be ignored by Gyokeres and his camp”. For a centre-forward already fighting for starts, that pursuit naturally sends a message, whether intended or not. It is also notable that Arsenal are said to be open to doing more business in attack. TeamTalk reports that the club “could be prepared to consider allowing Gyokeres to leave as they continue pushing ahead with plans to bring in another forward”. If that proves accurate, this is no longer a story about one unhappy player alone. It becomes a structural squad decision. Julian Alvarez interest adds to transfer pressure Arsenal “remain hugely keen on Alvarez”, according to the report, and that ongoing interest appears to be one of the two key drivers behind Gyokeres’ current stance, along with the absence of Premier League starts. item.content:encoded: Arsenal star pushing for January exit after recent struggles Viktor Gyokeres and Arsenal Facing January Crossroads as Exit Talk Grows Arsenal may be heading towards one of the most awkward transfer subplots of the coming window, with Viktor Gyokeres increasingly unsettled and a January move now described as a genuine possibility. According to TeamTalk , the Sweden international is prepared to reassess his future after a rapid change in standing under Mikel Arteta. The striking part of this developing story is the speed of the shift. Gyokeres arrived from Sporting CP in 2025 amid significant expectation, after Arsenal chose him ahead of Benjamin Sesko. He then delivered in a major way, scoring 21 goals in all competitions, including 14 in the Premier League, and playing his part in a title-winning season as well as a run to the Champions League final. That return should have strengthened his place. Instead, the current picture appears very different. TeamTalk states that “Viktor Gyokeres is ready to quit Arsenal and is set to push for a January exit”, a line that underlines the seriousness of the situation. The report adds that frustration over his minutes is central, with the striker “yet to start a Premier League game this season”. Premier League starts at centre of Arsenal concern From the player’s perspective, the issue seems straightforward. A striker of Gyokeres’ profile and age does not want to drift through the first half of a season waiting for opportunities. Sources cited in the report say “his lack of opportunities is the main reason he is now looking towards the exit door”, and there is little ambiguity in that. Photo IMAGO Arsenal’s internal thinking may be more layered. Kai Havertz is “currently the preferred option”, while long-term admiration for Julian Alvarez remains active in the background. The report notes that Arsenal’s pursuit of Alvarez over the summer was “a development that could not be ignored by Gyokeres and his camp”. For a centre-forward already fighting for starts, that pursuit naturally sends a message, whether intended or not. It is also notable that Arsenal are said to be open to doing more business in attack. TeamTalk reports that the club “could be prepared to consider allowing Gyokeres to leave as they continue pushing ahead with plans to bring in another forward”. If that proves accurate, this is no longer a story about one unhappy player alone. It becomes a structural squad decision. Julian Alvarez interest adds to transfer pressure Arsenal “remain hugely keen on Alvarez”, according to the report, and that ongoing interest appears to be one of the two key drivers behind Gyokeres’ current stance, along with the absence of Premier League starts. In practical terms, a striker can accept competition. What becomes harder to accept is the sense that the club may already be planning for somebody else to lead the line. That is why this situation feels significant. Arsenal “spent months doing their homework on Gyokeres” before completing the move, and Arteta had been clear in wanting him in north London. For that level of planning to lead to this uncertainty little more than a year later would raise fair questions over recruitment alignment and squad planning. Gyokeres has done his part internationally, too. He “continues to score regularly for Sweden and struck four goals during the recent Nations League international break”. That form only sharpens the player’s likely belief that he should be starting more often at club level. Atletico Madrid and Europe monitoring Gyokeres situation As for the market, Atletico Madrid remain firmly in the frame. TeamTalk says the Spanish club’s interest was discussed directly with Arsenal during meetings involving Andrea Berta in the summer. There is also mention of interest from the Premier League, Italy and Germany, suggesting this is not a case of one option or nothing. Crucially, the pieces do appear to fit. The report says “with the player open to a departure and the club still keen to strengthen their attacking options, a January separation could suit both parties”. That may ultimately be the clearest line in the entire update. If both sides see logic in a split, the coming months could be about shaping the right deal rather than preventing an exit. Arsenal still have time to change the direction of this story. More starts, a clearer role and firmer communication would help. For now, though, Viktor Gyokeres, Arsenal and a possible January transfer are moving into a space worth watching very closely. Our View From an Arsenal supporter’s perspective, this is deeply frustrating because it feels like a familiar problem of our own making. We signed a striker with pedigree, backed him after a long process, watched him score 21 goals in a huge season, then somehow reached a point where “the striker is yet to start a Premier League game this season”. That is hard to defend. If the report is accurate, the most annoying part is the mixed messaging. You cannot push for a player, pick him ahead of other targets, celebrate the decision, then spend the next window chasing another elite forward and expect there to be no consequences. Of course Gyokeres and his camp would question where he stands. Any player would. There is also a bigger concern for Arsenal here. Elite clubs need strong competition, but they also need clarity. If Kai Havertz is the preferred option, say it through selection. If Gyokeres is genuinely valued, use him properly. Letting a proven goalscorer slide towards the exit after one strong season would feel wasteful and short-sighted. Supporters will rightly ask why a player who helped deliver the title now seems expendable so quickly. If Arsenal sell in January and then spend heavily again, it will look like another expensive correction rather than a clear plan. That is the part fans will struggle with most.

item.title: Venezia upset Napoli for first Serie A win of season
item.description: Venezia goalkeeper saves a penalty from Napoli's Kevin de Bruyne (ANDREA PATTARO) Napoli's torrid start to the season continued Saturday when Venezia head coach Davide Nicola masterminded a shock 1-0 win on debut as Kevin De Bruyne had a penalty saved. Renowned survival specialist Nicola was appointed during the week to replace sacked coach Giovanni Stroppa after last season's Serie B champions failed to pick up a single point in their opening six games. He made an instant impact as Akor Adams struck the winner early in the second half to seal Venezia's first Serie A win over Napoli since 1942. It marked a second defeat in a row for Massimiliano Allegri's side after their midweek Champions League loss at Villarreal, and their fifth defeat in nine games in all competitions this season. A flat game came to life early in the second half when Nigeria international Adams latched on to a long ball and beat Alex Meret with a deflected strike in the 49th minute. Allegri responded by bringing on rested stars Rasmus Hojlund and Kevin De Bruyne and the Danish striker immediately threatened when Juan Jesus denied him a tap-in with a superb goal-line block. Hojlund won a penalty for Napoli midway through the second half when he was hauled down in the box by Matias Moreno, but De Bruyne's spot-kick was well saved by Filip Stankovic low to his right. The Venezia goalkeeper, son of former Inter midfielder Dejan Stankovic, was decisive in the closing stages with a string of saves, including spectacular stops to deny Stanislav Lobotka and Alisson Santos. Napoli are ninth after picking up 10 points from their first seven games, while Venezia remain bottom with three points. Later on Saturday, league leaders Inter travel to Bologna before Roma host Genoa. str/pb

item.title: NFL draft prospects 2027: Players to watch for Florida State vs. Miami
item.description: CLEMSON, SOUTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 03: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes warms up during the first half of a football game against the Clemson Tigers at Memorial Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Clemson, South Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 7 of the college football season is here, and it brings a key Florida in-state rivalry game. The Florida State Seminoles head from Tallahassee to South Florida today to face the Miami Hurricanes. This game obviously has plenty of meaning for our community, with so many people having attended or become fans of either team. It felt like the right time to bring in the Miami Dolphins’ perspective and take a closer look at some of the 2027 NFL Draft prospects who could be on the field today. The game kicks off at 7 p.m. Eastern on ESPN and Disney+. Florida State 2027 Draft prospects Duce Robinson, wide receiver (Senior) – Robinson is a huge target – like a bigger-than-the-Dolphins-tight-ends huge target. Listed at 6-foot-6 and 230 pounds, Robinson uses his size to give his quarterback a receiver who will fight for contested passes in a huge catch radius. If he gets his hands on the ball, it is going to be a catch. He is not the most precise route runner, and he does not have the speed to pull away from anyone, so he relies on his size to make the catch rather than speed to create separation. He is probably a day-two prospect who can excel as a possession receiver and redzone target. Charles Lester III, cornerback (Junior) – Lester is likely a developmental outside cornerback with good size. He is 6-foot-2 and 195 pounds, but he still needs to develop his technique, especially against faster, smaller wide receivers. He needs to clean up his work when receivers cut, but he can coach that up this year and in the NFL. He still has eligibility, so a 2027 return to college is not out of the question, but he could transition to the league, probably as a day-two pick. For Miami, where cornerback depth is a question mark, Lester could be an ideal option. Ja’Bril Rawls, cornerback (Senior) – Another cornerback with good size (6-foot-1, 180 pounds), Rawls is behind his teammate in draft potential, but the potential for success in the NFL is there. He probably needs to add strength, and his frame suggests he can do that without sacrificing speed. He has the versatility to slide back to safety, which might be the better option. He is not the best tackler, and he will need to clean that up in the NFL, especially if he is expected to step up in run defense. A developmental defensive back option who should contribute on special teams, Rawls is likely a day-three prospect who could rise to the end of day two. Quintrevion Wisner, running back (Senior) – The former Texas running back moved to Florida State this year after three seasons in Austin. He carried the ball 226 times for 1,064 yards in 2024, but he played only nine games in 2025 due to a hamstring injury. He has 29 carries for 141 yar
item.content:encoded: CLEMSON, SOUTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 03: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes warms up during the first half of a football game against the Clemson Tigers at Memorial Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Clemson, South Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 7 of the college football season is here, and it brings a key Florida in-state rivalry game. The Florida State Seminoles head from Tallahassee to South Florida today to face the Miami Hurricanes. This game obviously has plenty of meaning for our community, with so many people having attended or become fans of either team. It felt like the right time to bring in the Miami Dolphins’ perspective and take a closer look at some of the 2027 NFL Draft prospects who could be on the field today. The game kicks off at 7 p.m. Eastern on ESPN and Disney+. Florida State 2027 Draft prospects Duce Robinson, wide receiver (Senior) – Robinson is a huge target – like a bigger-than-the-Dolphins-tight-ends huge target. Listed at 6-foot-6 and 230 pounds, Robinson uses his size to give his quarterback a receiver who will fight for contested passes in a huge catch radius. If he gets his hands on the ball, it is going to be a catch. He is not the most precise route runner, and he does not have the speed to pull away from anyone, so he relies on his size to make the catch rather than speed to create separation. He is probably a day-two prospect who can excel as a possession receiver and redzone target. Charles Lester III, cornerback (Junior) – Lester is likely a developmental outside cornerback with good size. He is 6-foot-2 and 195 pounds, but he still needs to develop his technique, especially against faster, smaller wide receivers. He needs to clean up his work when receivers cut, but he can coach that up this year and in the NFL. He still has eligibility, so a 2027 return to college is not out of the question, but he could transition to the league, probably as a day-two pick. For Miami, where cornerback depth is a question mark, Lester could be an ideal option. Ja’Bril Rawls, cornerback (Senior) – Another cornerback with good size (6-foot-1, 180 pounds), Rawls is behind his teammate in draft potential, but the potential for success in the NFL is there. He probably needs to add strength, and his frame suggests he can do that without sacrificing speed. He has the versatility to slide back to safety, which might be the better option. He is not the best tackler, and he will need to clean that up in the NFL, especially if he is expected to step up in run defense. A developmental defensive back option who should contribute on special teams, Rawls is likely a day-three prospect who could rise to the end of day two. Quintrevion Wisner, running back (Senior) – The former Texas running back moved to Florida State this year after three seasons in Austin. He carried the ball 226 times for 1,064 yards in 2024, but he played only nine games in 2025 due to a hamstring injury. He has 29 carries for 141 yards this season, but is buried on the depth chart, and he has to prove he can be a receiving option out of the backfield before he can be considered a feature running back at the NFL level. He is a day-three depth running back option who can contribute on special teams. Micahi Danzy, wide receiver (Redshirt sophomore) – Danzy is the smaller receiver on our FSU prospects list, but that is only because Robinson is ridiculously large. Danzy is listed at 6-foot-1 and 195 pounds, and he can line up in multiple roles among the receiving corps. He has track speed, setting the FSU school record in the 400, and started his college career as a running back. He has 19 receptions for 139 yards and two touchdowns this season. He uses his speed to his advantage but needs to keep building his route tree. He is probably a day-three prospect who could use his speed to battle his way into a day-two consideration. Miami 2027 Draft prospects Darian Mensah, quarterback (Redshirt junior) – Mensah is a modern college football player who bounces between teams; he started at Tulane, then spent a year at Duke before moving to Miami this year. He throws with anticipation and makes good decisions, but he does not always work through his progressions and still has to prove he can handle pressure. He does not have the strongest arm and throws great short-to-medium passes, but the ball can die on longer throws at times. He could be the first quarterback off the board this year, potentially as the number one overall pick. Xavier Lucas, cornerback (Junior) – Lucas might be the ideal press-corner for the NFL. He has the size (6-foot-2, 200 pounds) to disrupt receivers at the line of scrimmage and the speed to keep up with the league’s vertical threats. He contests passes well, using his size to break up jump balls, but he is more likely to knock the ball away than to come away with an interception. He is a liability on run defense, with seemingly no interest in getting his nose into the mess in front of him; he also needs to clean up his tackling. Lucas has missed the last month of the season with an undisclosed injury, but he is expected to return for tonight’s game. He is probably a day-two prospect who is clearly not a finished product and will continue to grow in the NFL. For a Dolphins team in need of defensive secondary help, Lucas could be a key target. Note: Lucas is the basis of the lawsuit from Wisconsin against Miami. Lucas played his freshman year at Wisconsin under a two-year Name, Image, and Likeness contract. He tried to transfer to Miami for his second season, but Wisconsin refused to enter him into the transfer portal, citing his contract. Lucas dropped out of Wisconsin and enrolled at Miami without entering the NCAA’s transfer portal, and Wisconsin is alleging tampering by Miami to entice Lucas to transfer. Damon Wilson II, edge (Senior) – The Dolphins will likely be highly interested in edge rushers in the 2027 Draft, and Wilson could put himself on the board. At 6-foot-4 and 250 pounds, Wilson has the size and athleticism needed to succeed in the NFL. He uses both speed and power to attack offensive tackles, but he needs to add counter moves to get off the block if his initial move does not win. He also needs to improve his edge-setting against the run. He has the flashes to be great in the NFL, but he hasn’t shown the consistency yet. He broke out last year at Missouri with a nine-sack season, and he has tallied 3.5 sacks through the first five games this year, including 2.5 sacks against Clemson a couple of weeks ago. If he can keep up that production, he will be a second-round target who could slide into the end of the first round. Samson Okunlola, offensive tackle/guard (Redshirt Junior) – Okunlola’s potential is projected based on limited playing time at Miami. He did not get regular snaps until last year, when he rotated at left guard all season. He was clean, did not allow a sack, and showed he could be relied on in big spots. He slid out to left tackle this year, and he has been successful there as well – though he has had a penalty issue that needs to be cleaned up. He could bring that versatility to the NFL, allowing teams to use him as either a guard or tackle as needed. At 6-foot-6, 330 pounds, he still brings athleticism to the line and could be an effective mover to lead block in running situations. He is probably a day-two prospect who could start as a depth option at tackle and guard before settling into a starting role as a guard on the line. Ryan Rodriguez, center (Redshirt Senior) – A sixth-year college player, Rodriguez has played both guard and center at Miami. He has had injury issues, including needing surgery in 2022 and 2024. He is 6-foot-2 and 300 pounds, which is smaller than most NFL interior linemen, but Miami’s All-Pro center, Aaron Brewer, is 6-foot-2 and 290 pounds, so that might not be a major concern. He has to prove he can withstand the pressure of an entire season and ancho

item.title: Confirmed: Barcelona starting lineup against Real Betis – 4 changes as Flick rotates ahead of PSG
item.description: Confirmed: Barcelona starting lineup against Real Betis – 4 changes as Flick rotates ahead of PSG FC Barcelona are set to take on Real Betis at La Cartuja in La Liga in less than an hour and Hansi Flick has announced his starting lineup for this evening’s encounter. The Catalans enter the contest looking to maintain their perfect start to the league campaign, having won all eight matches so far this season. However, the fixture comes during an exceptionally demanding period for Barcelona, following their 4-1 Champions League victory over Galatasaray. It is sandwiched right inbetween that trip to Turkey and a trip to France to face PSG, before welcoming Real Madrid to the Camp Nou next weekend. Flick’s team selection has attracted particular attention, with the German tactician having to make some difficult calls to manage workload. Flick makes 4 changes against Betis In goal, Joan Garcia unsurprisingly starts for Barcelona, while Jules Kounde, Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin and Xavi Espart complete the defensive line. Moving into midfield, Rodri and Pedri feature alongside Fermin Lopez as Flick looks to establish control against a Betis side capable of causing problems in possession. Further forward, Lamine Yamal and Karim Adeyemi occupy the wide positions with Gabriel Jesus leading Barca’s attack. The most notable selection decision is starting Karim Adeyemi on the left instead of the in-form Anthony Gordon. Meanwhile, Jules Kounde replaces Eric at right-back and Gabriel Jesus returns to the starting line-up after a promising cameo against Galatasaray. With Barcelona facing PSG and Real Madrid in the coming days, Flick’s choices also offer an indication of how he intends to manage his squad through this important run of fixtures. Nevertheless, the immediate priority remains securing another three points and extending Barcelona’s outstanding start to the domestic season and it remains to be seen how they fare against Betis.

item.title: Fantasy Football Injury Alert: A.J. Brown Expected to Play Week 6; Fantasy Fallout for Drake Maye and Patriots
item.description: Sep 9, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; aNew England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (1) runs a route against Seattle Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe (29) during the second quarter at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A.J. Brown's Impending Return Changes Fantasy Landscape in New England Fantasy managers who invested heavily in the New England Patriots' passing game this offseason have spent the last month and a half navigating a turbulent landscape. When blockbuster offseason acquisition A.J. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain in the opening quarter of Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks, it felt like a cruel joke. Sidelined on Injured Reserve for the better part of two months, Brown left fantasy lineups scrambling and forced a heavy burden onto a patchwork receiving corps. Now, according to reports from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the dark cloud is lifting. The Patriots are expected to activate Brown off Injured Reserve in time for their divisional matchup against the New York Jets. After returning to practice this week and testing his ankle, the star wideout is poised to reclaim his role as the undisputed fantasy stud wide receiver of this offense. While Brown may have a bit of a pitch count that limits his upside to more of a WR2 this week, his fantasy managers absolutely have to start him. The #Patriots will likely activate WR AJ Brown off Injured Reserve to play against the #Jets on Sunday, sources say. Brown returned to practice this week after a stint on IR with a high-ankle sprain and now an anticipated return to the field. pic.twitter.com/UknZRnrv8T - Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 17, 2026 For fantasy football players, this news is an absolute earthquake. Inserting an elite, difference-making alpha back into an active offense changes the math across the entire roster. item.content:encoded: Sep 9, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; aNew England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (1) runs a route against Seattle Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe (29) during the second quarter at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A.J. Brown's Impending Return Changes Fantasy Landscape in New England Fantasy managers who invested heavily in the New England Patriots' passing game this offseason have spent the last month and a half navigating a turbulent landscape. When blockbuster offseason acquisition A.J. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain in the opening quarter of Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks, it felt like a cruel joke. Sidelined on Injured Reserve for the better part of two months, Brown left fantasy lineups scrambling and forced a heavy burden onto a patchwork receiving corps. Now, according to reports from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the dark cloud is lifting. The Patriots are expected to activate Brown off Injured Reserve in time for their divisional matchup against the New York Jets. After returning to practice this week and testing his ankle, the star wideout is poised to reclaim his role as the undisputed fantasy stud wide receiver of this offense. While Brown may have a bit of a pitch count that limits his upside to more of a WR2 this week, his fantasy managers absolutely have to start him. The #Patriots will likely activate WR AJ Brown off Injured Reserve to play against the #Jets on Sunday, sources say. Brown returned to practice this week after a stint on IR with a high-ankle sprain and now an anticipated return to the field. pic.twitter.com/UknZRnrv8T - Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 17, 2026 For fantasy football players, this news is an absolute earthquake. Inserting an elite, difference-making alpha back into an active offense changes the math across the entire roster. But how does this dramatic shift impact key offensive pieces like Drake Maye, Romeo Doubs, Hunter Henry, and Demario Douglas? Let's break down the fantasy fallout for Week 6. Fantasy Football Fallout Oct 11, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (10) throws a pass against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second half at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect QB Drake Maye, New England Patriots For young quarterback Drake Maye, the return of his premier weapon provides an invaluable ceiling boost. Maye has experienced a bumpy start to the season while leaning on a patchwork receiving corps, but a route-running technician of Brown's caliber offers the ultimate safety valve and field-stretcher. With opposing defenses forced to dedicate heavy safety attention to Brown, Maye will benefit from wider throwing windows and softer underneath zones. While Maye has been one of the best fantasy quarterbacks over the last two weeks, his overall upside skyrockets now that he possesses a legitimate go-to option capable of turning simple plays into explosive gains. He has legit overall QB1 upside this week. WR Romeo Doubs, New England Patriots Romeo Doubs saw an expanded target share in Brown's absence, but the production has been erratic. With Brown drawing the primary cornerback coverage, Doubs slides back into a more natural secondary role. While he will face lighter defensive coverages, his total target volume will likely decrease, converting him into a high-upside, boom-or-bust flex play for Week 6. TE Hunter Henry, New England Patriots Hunter Henry occupies a uniquely stable position amid this offensive reshuffle. Henry has quietly maintained reliable chemistry with Maye throughout the early weeks of the season, and Brown's presence on the perimeter should only help the veteran tight end. Elite wide receivers stretch defenses both vertically and laterally, opening up lucrative soft spots in the middle of the field where tight ends thrive. Henry retains his status as a steady back-end option, with his red-zone equity actually getting a boost because defenses can no longer focus solely on bracketing tight ends and slot receivers near the goal line. Consider Henry a high-end TE2 with TE1 upside this week. WR Demario Douglas, New England Patriots Meanwhile, Demario Douglas faces a more noticeable PPR floor dip. Douglas thrived on manufactured touches and short-area slot volume while the receiving room was decimated, but Brown's return eats directly into those underneath targets, turning Douglas into a game-script-dependent flex play or roster hold. Douglas belongs on the bench outside of deep fantasy leagues this week, and can be thrown back on the waiver wire in most leagues. Latest Fantasy Football News Week 6 Fantasy Football Final Injury Report: AJ Brown, Quinshon Judkins, And Updates On All The Top Stars Fantasy Football Injury Alert: Tyler Warren Managers Need to Have a TE Streamer Ready for Week 6 DeVonta Smith Is Set To Return From Injury, But Is He A Fantasy Football Start With Jalen Hurts OUT? Josh Jacobs To Be Removed From The Commissioner's Exempt List And In Fantasy Football Lineups As Soon As Week 7 This article was originally published on www.si.com/onsi/fantasy as Fantasy Football Injury Alert: A.J. Brown Expected to Play Week 6; Fantasy Fallout for Drake Maye and Patriots .

item.title: In-form Atletico snatch late win at Espanyol
item.description: Alex Baena struck in the 89th minute to snatch Atletico Madrid a 1-0 win at Espanyol and put pressure on La Liga leaders Barcelona on Saturday. Diego Simeone’s side, second, moved two points behind Hansi Flick’s champions, who visit third-placed Real Betis later on. Spain international Baena smashed home from the edge of the box to claim the Rojiblancos an important late victory from a tight game in Cornella. Atletico have won six consecutive games across all competitions. “They had a good game defensively and it was hard for us,” Baena told DAZN. “The good thing this team has is that it keeps believing until the 90th minute.” Baena, who struggled last season but has been in fine fettle since winning the World Cup with Spain this summer, hugged coach Simeone after finding the net. “He’s a player who can do a lot of damage, who is in very good form,” Simeone told DAZN after Baena’s fifth league goal of the season. Both sides had chances in the first half but Espanyol came closest as Leandro Cabrera struck the crossbar. Marcos Llorente hit the same woodwork after an hour with a long-range effort for Atletico. Espanyol brought on captain Javi Puado after a long-term knee injury, as he made his first appearance since January. Julian Alvarez was bright for Atletico as a substitute as he continues to find his form after trying to force a move away in the summer. Atletico have left it late several times this season to claim points and did so again here, with Baena thumping home from Alvarez’s pass to earn his team’s victory. “Last year (Baena) started well but then injuries prevented him from reaching his best form and having the season he wanted,” Simeone told reporters. “The World Cup took him to a different place, he sees football differently than others and (now) he’s more confident and stronger, he’s the player we went looking for.” Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak made a good save in stoppage time from Pol Lozano to ensure his team kept the three points. On Sunday Real Madrid, fourth, host Sevilla among other fixtures. AFP The post In-form Atletico snatch late win at Espanyol appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lawyers fault demand for deposits before emergency treatment of patients
item.description: Some Lagos-based lawyers on Saturday, warned hospitals and healthcare providers against demanding upfront payments before treating patients in medical emergencies. The lawyers told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) that such actions violate the National Health Act of 2014, and attract legal sanctions. They argue that section 20(1) of the Act prohibited healthcare providers, health workers and health establishments from refusing emergency medical treatment for any reason, including a patient’s inability to pay a deposit. The lawyers, however, called for effective healthcare financing and reimbursement mechanisms, to protect hospitals from financial losses while ensuring that patients received timely medical attention. An Associate of the Institute of Medical and Health Law, Ms Odinichionye Egwuenu, told NAN that the law was clear that emergency treatment must not be withheld because a patient could not make upfront payment. Egwuenu said the provision applied to both public and private hospitals, noting that internal hospital policies could not override statutory obligations. She, however, urged stakeholders to consider the financial challenges facing healthcare institutions, including staff salaries, equipment maintenance and the procurement of medications. According to her, the situation becomes more complicated when a hospital provides emergency treatment but the patient dies and the family subsequently abandons the deceased or refuses to settle the outstanding medical bills. “We must also consider the practical realities of healthcare delivery; Hospitals have staff to pay, equipment to maintain and medications to purchase. “So, while human life must take priority in an emergency, what happens when a hospital provides treatment, the patient dies despite its efforts, and the family abandons the deceased,” she said While noting that section 11 of the National Health Act established the Basic Health Care Provision Fund, she said that the effectiveness of such funding required clos examination to determine whether hospitals received adequate support for emergency services. Meanwhile, she also drew attention to the Compulsory Treatment and Care for Victims of Gunshot Act, 2017, which requires hospitals to treat gunshot victims without demanding deposits or insisting on police clearance. She urged hospitals to notify the nearest police station within two hours of commencing treatment in compliance with the law, The lawyer also called for institutional safeguards to protect medical practitioners who disregarded internal payment policies to fulfil their professional obligations to emergency patients. She, consequently, called for the strengthening of emergency healthcare funding, establishing effective reimbursement mechanisms as well as providing lawful avenues for recovering outstanding medical expenses. On his part, another lawyer, Mr Spurgeon Ataene, said doctors had an ethical obligation to prioritise saving lives in emergency situations before turn

The lawyers told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) that such actions violate the National Health Act of 2014, and attract legal sanctions. They argue that section 20(1) of the Act prohibited healthcare providers, health workers and health establishments from refusing emergency medical treatment for any reason, including a patient’s inability to pay a deposit. The lawyers, however, called for effective healthcare financing and reimbursement mechanisms, to protect hospitals from financial losses while ensuring that patients received timely medical attention. An Associate of the Institute of Medical and Health Law, Ms Odinichionye Egwuenu, told NAN that the law was clear that emergency treatment must not be withheld because a patient could not make upfront payment. Egwuenu said the provision applied to both public and private hospitals, noting that internal hospital policies could not override statutory obligations. She, however, urged stakeholders to consider the financial challenges facing healthcare institutions, including staff salaries, equipment maintenance and the procurement of medications. According to her, the situation becomes more complicated when a hospital provides emergency treatment but the patient dies and the family subsequently abandons the deceased or refuses to settle the outstanding medical bills. “We must also consider the practical realities of healthcare delivery; Hospitals have staff to pay, equipment to maintain and medications to purchase. “So, while human life must take priority in an emergency, what happens when a hospital provides treatment, the patient dies despite its efforts, and the family abandons the deceased,” she said While noting that section 11 of the National Health Act established the Basic Health Care Provision Fund, she said that the effectiveness of such funding required clos examination to determine whether hospitals received adequate support for emergency services. Meanwhile, she also drew attention to the Compulsory Treatment and Care for Victims of Gunshot Act, 2017, which requires hospitals to treat gunshot victims without demanding deposits or insisting on police clearance. She urged hospitals to notify the nearest police station within two hours of commencing treatment in compliance with the law, The lawyer also called for institutional safeguards to protect medical practitioners who disregarded internal payment policies to fulfil their professional obligations to emergency patients. She, consequently, called for the strengthening of emergency healthcare funding, establishing effective reimbursement mechanisms as well as providing lawful avenues for recovering outstanding medical expenses. On his part, another lawyer, Mr Spurgeon Ataene, said doctors had an ethical obligation to prioritise saving lives in emergency situations before turning their attention to payment. Ataene said demanding payment before attending to a patient in a life-threatening condition, could amount to professional misconduct and potentially expose the practitioner to disciplinary action. He added that denying emergency care on financial grounds could also raise concerns about the patient’s fundamental right to life. Ataene specifically stressed that gunshot victims should be treated before questions were asked about the circumstances of their injuries. “It will therefore, be unethical for a doctor to make a demand for payment before treatment; He could be sanctioned and may lose his license,” he said Ataene, however, acknowledged that patients should pay for medical services, particularly in non-emergency situations, noting that hospitals required funds to maintain equipment, pay staff and provide a clean and orderly environment. He urged lawmakers to strengthen legislation requiring healthcare providers to stabilise emergency patients before making payment demands or conducting further inquiries that could delay treatment. Similarly, another Lagos-based lawyer, Mrs Jumoke Ajayi of Olorunwapelumi Chambers, warned that healthcare providers could face criminal sanctions for refusing emergency medical treatment over unpaid bills. Ajayi cited Section 20(2) of the National Health Act, which prescribes a fine of N100,000, imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months, or both, for contravening the provision on emergency medical treatment. She explained that patients suffering from serious injuries sustained in road accidents, severe bleeding or other life-threatening conditions were entitled to immediate medical attention, irrespective of their financial circumstances. “The legal position is that the hospital must attend to the patient’s emergency medical needs without refusing treatment on financial grounds,” she said. Ajayi, however, clarified that the law did not automatically exempt patients from paying their medical bills, adding that hospitals could subsequently seek payment for services provided, subject to applicable laws and relevant payment arrangements. According to her, determining whether a hospital or healthcare worker had committed an offence would depend on the circumstances and available evidence, including whether treatment was refused, delayed or referred to another facility. Meanwhile, Ajayi noted that healthcare workers could not be held liable for consequences arising from their inability to provide particular emergency services where a hospital lacked the necessary equipment or capacity to handle the case. Besides, she noted that the law protected patients’ access to emergency care but did not require every form of medical treatment to be provided free of charge. On the whole, the lawyers maintained that protecting patients’ lives and sustaining healthcare institutions should not be competing objectives. They consequently, urging government and relevant stakeholders to develop a system that guarantees emergency treatment while providing hospitals with adequate financial support. NAN The post Lawyers fault demand for deposits before emergency treatment of patients appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 22 Years Ago, One Perfect Twist Changed TV's Greatest Sci-Fi Series Forever
item.description: At the time, Lindelof was discussing his new series, Lost — which just four episodes in, had pulled off a mind-blowing twist arguably on the same level as The Sixth Sense . For its first few episodes, Lost seems like an ambitious survival drama with a dash of horror. Oceanic Flight 815 crashes on a seemingly deserted tropical island. Its survivors contend with dwindling supplies, a rampaging monster, an inexplicable polar bear, and the unfortunate realization that rescuers are probably searching a thousand miles away from where they actually crashed.

item.title: Pikmin 4 is $20 off ahead of its $10 Nintendo Switch 2 update
item.description: Pikmin preparing to do battle with a Bulborb | Image: Nintendo If you’re wondering what video game to play this weekend, my colleague Sheena Vasani spotted a discounted Nintendo Switch title with instant digital delivery. Walmart has the digital version of Pikmin 4 for Switch discounted to $39.88, just over $20 lower than its usual price. This version of the game follows the same puzzle formula as previous titles in the series, but adds in a dog companion for an extra layer of complexity and action, and dives deeper into the dark undertones previous games hinted at. Pikmin 4 Where to Buy: $59.99 $39.88 at Walmart Nintendo recently announced a Switch 2 version of Pikmin 4 will launch on November 12th, 2026. That version features polished visuals, adds in voice commands for your dog companion, plus a new mode called Dandori Academy that adds extra challenges over time. You’ll be able to upgrade to that version for just $10, saving you $20 total over buying the $69.99 Switch 2 Edition outright. Read our Pikmin 4 review .
