item.title: Egypt’s president says country ready to defend Saudi Arabia ‘if requested’
item.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Saturday said Egypt was ready to defend Saudi Arabia “if requested”, as fighting flares between the kingdom and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. Since Yemen’s war reignited in July, the Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week. The Houthis have also blockaded the Bab al-Mandab Strait, piling pressure on energy exports as Iran presses its own blockade on the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian military academy, Sisi said Egypt was “not looking for a role to play” in regional conflicts, but added that it was “inconceivable” for Cairo to stand by while Saudi Arabia was “harmed or its security and stability threatened”. “Egypt, of course, with the directives of His Majesty King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will carry out any measure to protect you or defend you,” he said. He added that any deployment would require parliamentary approval and said he hoped lawmakers would convene in an emergency session to grant authorisation “if it is requested of us”. “I’m not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone,” Sisi said. “We are speaking only about defence.” During a visit to Egypt last month, de facto Saudi leader Mohammed bin Salman and Sisi called for free and secure navigation in the Red Sea, a vital trade route. The conflict with the Houthis poses risks not only to Saudi Arabia’s security and energy exports, but also to Egypt, where disruption to Red Sea shipping could further reduce revenues from the Suez Canal, a key source of foreign currency. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said last month that Egypt’s Suez Canal lost about $11 billion in revenues since the Houthis began attacking commercial vessels following Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack on Israel. Despite its longstanding military ties with Gulf states, Egypt has not joined the Mecca agreement, a mutual defence pact signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan in August, with Cairo generally favouring diplomacy over participation in regional military alliances. Saudi Arabia has long been a key backer of Egypt, providing financial support after the 2013 ouster of Islamist late president Mohammed Morsi and during subsequent economic crises. The post Egypt’s president says country ready to defend Saudi Arabia ‘if requested’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion
item.description: null On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew. An upgraded Orbital ATK Antares rocket soars into the night sky over NASA's Wallops Flight Facility on Wallops Island, Virginia on Oct. 17, 2016. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) Why it mattered For the International Space Station to be able to sustain a continuous human occupancy, periodic cargo deliveries are needed. Russia fulfills part of this requirement with its Progress spacecraft, and both ESA (European Space Agency) and JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) have contributed with their Automated Transfer Vehicle (ATV) and H-II Transfer Vehicle (HTV), respectively. For its part, NASA contracted with Orbital (today, Northrop Grumman) and SpaceX to fly commercial resupply service missions. Both were needed to keep the U.S. operating segment of the station well supplied and with the science and research materials needed for the crew's work. Below is a video of the explosion Though adjustments can be made to go without one or more of these vehicles for a short period of time, the Progress, Cygnus and Dragon are key components of the ISS's continuous operation. So returning a vehicle to flight after a catastrophic exploration is important to well-being of the International Space Station program. As it happened, Antares would fly another 12 times before having to stand down again to be redesigned, but that is for a different This Day in Space entry. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

item.title: France: "We've seen extremely high tensions between protesters and law enforcement"
item.description: Protesters across France called for street demonstrations on Saturday against rising living costs. France 24's Antonia Kerrigan reports from Paris. "The march from here to Place de Clichy isn't set to start for another hour. However, we've seen it kicking off extremely early doors. It seems that what's happened is that police attempted to block the protesters from reaching Place de la République, and we saw the use of tear gas. We've seen people running with their masks on. We also saw the use of stun grenades."

item.title: 4 Asian countries Nigerians can visit without applying for visa before travel
item.description: Nigerian passport holders have a limited number of options for travelling to Asia without completing a traditional visa application before departure. However, some destinations offer visa-on-arrival facilities, allowing eligible visitors to obtain entry permits at designated airports. According to available 2026 travel information, the Maldives, Lebanon, Timor-Leste and Cambodia are among the Asian destinations reported to offer Nigerian travellers alternative entry arrangements. The conditions differ by country, and travellers should confirm their eligibility before booking flights. Here are four destinations worth considering. 1. Maldives The Maldives is an island country in the Indian Ocean, known for its white-sand beaches, turquoise waters and luxury resorts. Nigerian passport holders are reported to be eligible for a tourist visa on arrival, meaning they do not generally need to obtain a tourist visa from a Maldivian embassy before travelling. Visitors should prepare a valid passport, accommodation details, a return or onward ticket and evidence of sufficient funds, as required by the immigration authorities. The Maldives is an option for Nigerians seeking a beach holiday, honeymoon or short leisure trip. Travellers should confirm the current requirements with Maldives Immigration before departure. 2. Lebanon Lebanon, located on the eastern coast of the Mediterranean Sea, combines historic sites, mountain scenery and a distinctive food culture. According to the Lebanese Consulate in Lagos, Nigerian passport holders are eligible for a free visa on arrival at Beirut Rafic Hariri International Airport. The visa is valid for one month and may be extendable, subject to the applicable conditions. Travellers are advised to carry a passport valid for at least six months beyond their intended stay, a return flight reservation and proof of accommodation. Before travelling, Nigerians should also check current security advisories and confirm that entry arrangements remain in effect. 3. Timor-Leste Timor-Leste, also known as East Timor, is a Southeast Asian country occupying the eastern half of the island of Timor. Its customs authority states that visitors can generally obtain a visa on arrival when entering by air or sea, subject to the applicable requirements. The published tourist visa fee is US$30. Travellers should have a passport valid for at least six months, a return or onward ticket, accommodation arrangements and evidence of sufficient funds. Nigerians planning to visit should confirm the current admission requirements with Timor-Leste’s authorities before booking their journey. 4. Cambodia Cambodia is a Southeast Asian destination known for Angkor Wat, historic temples, cultural attractions and the capital city, Phnom Penh. Some travel guides list Cambodia among destinations where Nigerian passport holders may obtain a visa on arrival. However, Cambodia’s official e-visa portal also offers an online tourist visa, with a published fee of US$3

Some travel guides list Cambodia among destinations where Nigerian passport holders may obtain a visa on arrival. However, Cambodia’s official e-visa portal also offers an online tourist visa, with a published fee of US$30 and a stated processing time of three business days. Because the available information does not conclusively establish that Nigerian ordinary passport holders currently qualify for visa on arrival, travellers should verify their eligibility directly with Cambodian immigration authorities before departure. If a prior e-visa is required, Cambodia should not be described as a destination that Nigerians can visit without applying for a visa beforehand. The post 4 Asian countries Nigerians can visit without applying for visa before travel appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Analogue Brings Back Its Perfect SNES And Sega Genesis Replacements
item.description: As original hardware ages, playing retro games becomes less practical for many reasons. Analogue strives to keep retro games alive by providing modern hardware capable of running games that are decades old. It did so with the launch of the Super Nt and Mega Sg in 2017 and 2019, respectively. If you missed out on these systems back then, you now have another chance to acquire them with the release of their upgraded versions: the Super Nt+ and the Mega Sg+.

item.title: 2026 Has Been a Surprisingly Excellent Year for Shooters
item.description: All the way back in January, it seemed like 2026 might be a rough year for fans of shooters. Highguard ’s launch and almost immediate delaunch created an anxiety around the genre that was hard to shake. Scrutiny around Marathon in the lead-up to its launch doubled that uncertainty, leaving some to wonder if the shooter genre — at least in its trusty live-service form — was going out of fashion.

item.title: Nigeria’s poor population may be world’s largest, says EU envoy
item.description: …commits €45m aid By Folarin Kehinde The European Union (EU) Ambassador to Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), Gautier Mignot, has said Nigeria probably has the highest number of people living below the poverty threshold globally, describing poverty as one of the country’s biggest challenges. The envoy spoke in Abuja over the weekend at the 2026 International Day for the Eradication of Poverty, where he called for sustained efforts by the Federal Government, development partners and other stakeholders to address the country’s poverty crisis. “Today, Nigeria is probably the country in the world with the highest number of people living under the poverty threshold,” he said. Mignot also disclosed that the European Union had committed nearly €45m in humanitarian assistance to Nigeria in 2026, particularly to support conflict-affected and crisis-prone areas. He described poverty as a major concern for Nigeria’s international partners, stressing that it required urgent attention and sustained commitment in the years ahead. Mignot cited figures indicating that 133 million Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty in 2022, adding that estimates from different sources suggested the situation had worsened since then. He said the EU’s humanitarian assistance was being provided through the European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations, with particular attention to communities affected by conflict and other crises. “Through the European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations, ECO, the European Union has committed again this year almost 45 million euros for humanitarian assistance in Nigeria, particularly in conflict-affected and crisis-prone areas”. According to him, the EU is working with the Nigerian government, humanitarian organisations, development partners and local communities to ensure that emergency assistance is linked to long-term resilience and sustainable solutions. He explained that humanitarian interventions address immediate needs, while poverty reduction programmes focus on creating lasting pathways out of poverty. Speaking on the theme of the event, United for Peace and Human Rights, Safe Homes for All, the ambassador said meaningful poverty reduction was impossible without peace, security, dignity and respect for human rights. He added that households unable to meet their basic needs could hardly feel secure or fully enjoy their fundamental rights. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: …commits €45m aid By Folarin Kehinde The European Union (EU) Ambassador to Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), Gautier Mignot, has said Nigeria probably has the highest number of people living below the poverty threshold globally, describing poverty as one of the country’s biggest challenges. The envoy spoke in Abuja over the weekend at the 2026 International Day for the Eradication of Poverty, where he called for sustained efforts by the Federal Government, development partners and other stakeholders to address the country’s poverty crisis. “Today, Nigeria is probably the country in the world with the highest number of people living under the poverty threshold,” he said. Mignot also disclosed that the European Union had committed nearly €45m in humanitarian assistance to Nigeria in 2026, particularly to support conflict-affected and crisis-prone areas. He described poverty as a major concern for Nigeria’s international partners, stressing that it required urgent attention and sustained commitment in the years ahead. Mignot cited figures indicating that 133 million Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty in 2022, adding that estimates from different sources suggested the situation had worsened since then. He said the EU’s humanitarian assistance was being provided through the European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations, with particular attention to communities affected by conflict and other crises. “Through the European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations, ECO, the European Union has committed again this year almost 45 million euros for humanitarian assistance in Nigeria, particularly in conflict-affected and crisis-prone areas”. According to him, the EU is working with the Nigerian government, humanitarian organisations, development partners and local communities to ensure that emergency assistance is linked to long-term resilience and sustainable solutions. He explained that humanitarian interventions address immediate needs, while poverty reduction programmes focus on creating lasting pathways out of poverty. Speaking on the theme of the event, United for Peace and Human Rights, Safe Homes for All, the ambassador said meaningful poverty reduction was impossible without peace, security, dignity and respect for human rights. He added that households unable to meet their basic needs could hardly feel secure or fully enjoy their fundamental rights. Mignot acknowledged the Federal Government’s efforts to tackle poverty through social investment programmes, targeted cash transfers, livelihood support and measures to strengthen social protection systems. He listed the National Social Safety Net Programme, the Nigeria Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus, and the Renewed Hope Social Protection Programme among the initiatives aimed at supporting vulnerable Nigerians. He also highlighted the Household Prosperity and Empowerment Social Protection Project, supported through Nigeria’s partnership with the World Bank, saying the initiative was expected to improve assistance to vulnerable households and strengthen their resilience. The envoy said the EU was complementing these efforts through its Supporting Sustainable Social Protection Systems in Nigeria programme, which works with government institutions and implementing partners, including UNICEF, GIZ, the International Labour Organisation, ActionAid and Oxfam. He disclosed that the programme covered Abia, Benue, Oyo, Sokoto, Kebbi, Adamawa and Borno states. According to him, the intervention focuses on strengthening social protection policies, expanding social registers to identify more poor and vulnerable households, and improving data systems for planning and resource allocation. Mignot said multidimensional poverty assessments helped governments identify overlapping deprivations in education, healthcare, nutrition and living standards, enabling them to target interventions more effectively. He added that the EU had supported the review of Nigeria’s National Social Protection Policy, as well as the development of state social protection policies and a Social Protection Bill. The ambassador also called for stronger coordination between humanitarian assistance and long-term development programmes, noting that poor households were particularly vulnerable to emergencies, including severe acute malnutrition. He welcomed the ongoing humanitarian transition, under which Nigerian authorities at all levels are expected to progressively assume greater responsibility for funding and coordinating humanitarian assistance. Mignot commended the minister responsible for humanitarian affairs and poverty reduction, Bernard Doro, for his efforts and reaffirmed the EU’s commitment to supporting Nigeria’s poverty reduction drive. He said tackling poverty sustainably required a coordinated, long-term approach involving government institutions, civil society, local communities and international development partners. “Humanitarian needs cannot wait, and poverty either,” he said, urging stakeholders to make the fight against poverty a year-round priority. The post Nigeria’s poor population may be world’s largest, says EU envoy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: CAN at 50: Church must challenge govt, defend Nigerians — Archbishop Okoh
item.description: …As First Lady urges Christians to sustain unity …Honours Gowon, OBJ, Osinbajo, others By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja President of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Archbishop Daniel Okoh, has charged the Church to challenge government failures, defend vulnerable Nigerians and resist political capture, declaring that it must not surrender its prophetic responsibility for the sake of political convenience. Speaking at CAN’s 50th anniversary celebration in Abuja on Saturday, Archbishop Okoh said the Church must adopt a more courageous, evidence-based and constructive approach to national affairs, holding those in power accountable while supporting policies that advance the common good. In his homily, themed “CAN at 50: A Prophetic Voice of Hope,” the CAN president said the Church must remain independent, morally alert and committed to speaking for Nigerians whose voices are often ignored. “The Church must speak!” he declared. Archbishop Okoh listed internally displaced persons, children denied education, unemployed youths, farmers unable to access their farmlands because of insecurity, women facing violence and victims of human trafficking among those whose plight the Church must address. He warned, however, that speaking prophetically did not mean opposing every government policy or turning the Church into a partisan platform. “A responsible watchman must be accurate. He should not raise alarm simply because he dislikes a policy or disagrees with a political leader,” he said. On the relationship between the Church and government, Archbishop Okoh advocated what he called critical collaboration, urging Christian leaders to commend good policies and challenge failures without compromising their independence. “Collaborate where common good requires it, challenge where justice requires challenge, commend where government does well and warn where government fails, while maintaining the Church’s independence,” he said. He said the next 50 years of CAN should be marked by stronger research, advocacy, institutional maturity and collective action, with greater attention to justice, human dignity, democratic institutions, religious freedom and the welfare of vulnerable citizens. Archbishop Okoh also urged Christians to preserve the unity that inspired CAN’s founding in August 1976, warning that denominational rivalries could weaken the Church’s collective voice. He recalled that the Association’s early years were marked by mutual suspicion and the marginalisation of some Christian traditions, but said successive leaders had worked to build a more inclusive platform. “At 50, all the church traditions in Nigeria are represented in CAN through the following major blocs: CSN, CCN, CPFN/PFN, OAIC and TEKAN/ECWA. The last time I checked, no one is missing on the table,” he said. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: …As First Lady urges Christians to sustain unity …Honours Gowon, OBJ, Osinbajo, others By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja President of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Archbishop Daniel Okoh, has charged the Church to challenge government failures, defend vulnerable Nigerians and resist political capture, declaring that it must not surrender its prophetic responsibility for the sake of political convenience. Speaking at CAN’s 50th anniversary celebration in Abuja on Saturday, Archbishop Okoh said the Church must adopt a more courageous, evidence-based and constructive approach to national affairs, holding those in power accountable while supporting policies that advance the common good. In his homily, themed “CAN at 50: A Prophetic Voice of Hope,” the CAN president said the Church must remain independent, morally alert and committed to speaking for Nigerians whose voices are often ignored. “The Church must speak!” he declared. Archbishop Okoh listed internally displaced persons, children denied education, unemployed youths, farmers unable to access their farmlands because of insecurity, women facing violence and victims of human trafficking among those whose plight the Church must address. He warned, however, that speaking prophetically did not mean opposing every government policy or turning the Church into a partisan platform. “A responsible watchman must be accurate. He should not raise alarm simply because he dislikes a policy or disagrees with a political leader,” he said. On the relationship between the Church and government, Archbishop Okoh advocated what he called critical collaboration, urging Christian leaders to commend good policies and challenge failures without compromising their independence. “Collaborate where common good requires it, challenge where justice requires challenge, commend where government does well and warn where government fails, while maintaining the Church’s independence,” he said. He said the next 50 years of CAN should be marked by stronger research, advocacy, institutional maturity and collective action, with greater attention to justice, human dignity, democratic institutions, religious freedom and the welfare of vulnerable citizens. Archbishop Okoh also urged Christians to preserve the unity that inspired CAN’s founding in August 1976, warning that denominational rivalries could weaken the Church’s collective voice. He recalled that the Association’s early years were marked by mutual suspicion and the marginalisation of some Christian traditions, but said successive leaders had worked to build a more inclusive platform. “At 50, all the church traditions in Nigeria are represented in CAN through the following major blocs: CSN, CCN, CPFN/PFN, OAIC and TEKAN/ECWA. The last time I checked, no one is missing on the table,” he said. The CAN president cautioned Christians against taking that unity for granted or allowing disagreements, particularly on social media, to undermine their fellowship. He stressed that CAN belonged to every believer, not just its elected and appointed officers, and urged members to break down remaining barriers between denominations. Drawing on the biblical image of a watchman, Archbishop Okoh said the Church had a duty to identify threats to justice and human dignity, warn those in authority and defend citizens whose circumstances left them vulnerable. He also called on Christians to match their prayers for Nigeria with practical action, integrity and responsible leadership. “Nigeria can be better — Nigeria will be better! But hope requires responsibility: prayer must be accompanied by positive action, faith by integrity, leadership by accountability and freedom by responsibility,” he said. Archbishop Okoh said the jubilee must serve as the beginning of a renewed national mission, with the Church expected to defend human dignity, demand accountability and contribute to national development. Christians Must Sustain Unity – Mrs Tinubu The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, congratulated CAN on its 50 years of service to God and humanity, urging Christian denominations to sustain their unity. She said the anniversary theme, “Walking Together in Faith,” reflected Christ’s prayer for the unity of believers. “I pray that, just as Christ prayed for the saints, all the Christian blocs and denominations will continue to remain united in Jesus’ name,” she said. The golden jubilee celebration also featured awards recognising prominent Nigerians and public office holders for their contributions to the Church and society. Honours as List Former Head of State, General Yakubu Gowon; former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo and Goodluck Jonathan; and former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo were listed among recipients of the Pillar of Faith awards. Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives Benjamin Kalu, Secretary to the Government of the Federation George Akume, several state governors and other public officials were listed in the Christian Icon category. The programme also featured prayers for Nigeria and its leaders, the presentation of CAN’s history book and the launch of a proposed airport chapel project. item.title: 6 scientifically accurate star projectors to turn any room into a home planetarium
item.description: Want to educate young children about the wonders of the cosmos? Depending on the time of year, your location and the weather, your hopes to see the night sky in real life might not be as easy as heading into the backyard and peering up. That's why one of the best star projectors might be the solution. That's why we've picked out six star projectors that actually deliver scientifically accurate images, from projections of the northern hemisphere to breathtaking pictures from the Hubble Space Telescope . Any one of these will turn your home into a private planetarium. Each comes with several swappable images, and you can purchase additional slides/discs for the Homestar and Pococo models. If you're seeking to stimulate a child's interest in space and STEM or just take your friends on a journey through space, these are the scientifically accurate projectors to purchase. item.dc:creator: Nilay Patel
item.content:encoded: Today, I’m talking with Walter Piecyk, a partner and analyst at LightShed Partners who covers tech, media, and telecom, about SpaceX’s recently announced plan to become a major wireless carrier. Last week, SpaceX agreed to buy a big chunk of low-band spectrum to expand the Starlink network, spectrum that’s been traded around the telecom business for decades now. SpaceX’s ambitious plan is to use that spectrum to help build “the world’s most advanced mobile network.” Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . Combined with news that the FCC approved the deployment of 15,000 next-gen Starlink satellites and the company’s previous agreement to purchase close to $20 billion worth of EchoStar spectrum last year, it’s now clear SpaceX is serious about competing with AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile. I’ve covered the telecom business for a long time, and I’ve always known that these companies can say they want to do something until they run into the harsh reality of how expensive it is to actually do it. The telecom graveyard of pivots, bad ideas, and failed acquisitions is vast. Walt has been closely monitoring SpaceX’s acquisition, and he’s correctly predicted that the company was headed in this direction for months now. So I wanted to dig into whether SpaceX can pull this off, why Walt thinks the existing telecom giants have really fumbled their response to SpaceX’s growing threat, and what happens when Elon Musk’s rocket company jumps headfirst into a business everyone loves to hate. Okay: LightShed Partners’ Walter Piecyk on SpaceX’s plan to expand into mobile. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Walter Piecyk, you’re a partner and a tech, media, and telecom analyst at LightShed Partners. Welcome to Decoder . Thanks for having me. I’m looking forward to it. I’m excited to talk to you. I feel like we’ve been tweeting or posting around each other for many, many years, but I’m a telecom nerd at heart. I’ve been covering the space for ages. SpaceX is going to make a big splash. It’s going to be the fourth major mobile carrier in the United States and maybe the world. It bought some spectrum to do it. It’s EchoStar spectrum by way of private equity. It is at once very simple and also very complicated. Give us the state of the state. SpaceX bought 800 Mhz spectrum for $8 billion . They spent nearly $20 billion already on separate EchoStar spectrum. What is SpaceX trying to do here? It’s definitely complicated, but maybe less complicated than trying to figure out how to put a data center out in space and making that work. Or something on the moon. But they don’t typically want to own spectrum and spend for spectrum. If you think about how Starlink was built, satellite companies don’t typically pay for spectrum. And then as the business evolved and as they saw the opportunity in telecom, they purchased some spectrum initially from EchoStar. The feedback they got from investors at that time was very positive and they said, “Wait a minute, you should do more here.” This is a trillion-dollar enterprise value business in the US alone. Obviously they have global aspirations both for Starlink as well as what they’re doing with this mobile telephone service. So they bought more. They went back to EchoStar. That’s a key thing to pay attention to, in that they bought some spectrum and then they went back and bought some more. Because with a lot of things that Elon Musk does, he learns as he goes. He bought the spectrum, got feedback, talked to people in telecom, and bought some more spectrum. Then we didn’t hear from them for a while. Now, you have this thing that happened last week where they bought some more spectrum, and I can go through the history of it if you care, but it’s long, wonky telecom stuff. This was originally the Nextel spectrum, if you remember that company. I do. Actually, I do want you to go through the history because I think the telecom business is best understood as a bunch of lobbyists trying to make everything more complicated than it should be. Yes, spectrum auctions are complicated and what spectrum is good for what is deeply tied to the physics of the radio spectrum and all that. But here it’s the 800 MHz spectrum from the Nextel service, the old push-to-talk, walkie-talkie service that Sprint had to divest as part of the deal to get sold to T-Mobile. They’ve been trying to sell it for ages. They sold it to this company, Grain Management. They’ve been sitting on it, and when Starlink showed up, Elon bought it. Nobody else wanted it. What did he see in the spectrum that no one else did? When you realize that you need to build a terrestrial network to support what you’re doing with satellites, because satellites work fine if you’ve got your dish on the top of your house and you’re getting your broadband, but when you’re trying to connect with a phone that doesn’t have the same type of power or you’re going inside a home, you’re going to need better coverage. Sirius Satellite also has supplementary towers. There are not that many of them, but sometimes when you get out of Sirius coverage, you will connect to a tower. When they bought that EchoStar spectrum and then got FCC approval, and if you looked into those details of that FCC approval and what was required, you would see that they can’t do this by satellites alone. There had to be terrestrial. Then SpaceX, as Elon is wont to do, tries to send some diversions like, “We’re going to do Femtocell, we’re not going to do macrocell, this, that, and the other thing.” But they realized that they were going to build a terrestrial network. Now they finally realized, “If I’m going to offer mobile service, I need some form of a terrestrial network.” At the same time, the telcos are not going to help them out. They’re not going to give them a wholesale agreement. Then when they go back and say the companies that had the lowest churn, what is the fundamental value you need in a terrestrial network? It’s low-band spectrum. Why? It travels further, you can get better coverage, and you have that connectivity. So getting this low-band spectrum piece was just an important part, not to make the satellites work better, but to actually give them the spectrum assets that they need to build a terrestrial network. That’s why the stocks reacted, because people finally came to terms with the fact that Elon is actually going to build a terrestrial network. I’m less interested in the stock and more interested in just the cost structure of how this works. If I rewind my brain to being a baby blogger at Engadget 100 years ago, the FCC told all the TV networks they had to stop broadcasting on 700 MHz and we were going to run an auction. Verizon and AT&T bought big chunks of 700 MHz spectrum and that’s what 4G is built on. That’s the low-bandwidth spectrum that you’re talking about. It goes everywhere. This was a big victory that we reallocated 700 MHz, and 800 MHz was sitting right there the whole time. This is the Nextel spectrum. If it is so valuable, why wasn’t there a market for it until Elon showed up just now? It was part of this transaction. T-Mobile ended up having to sell it because the government said, “If we’re going to allow you to take out the fourth competitor, which was Sprint, then in order to enable another fourth competitor out there, we need to have you guys give up some of your low-band spectrum.” Part of the deal that T-Mobile and Sprint had with the government was that they would sell it to EchoStar. Why? Because Charlie Ergen, CEO of Dish at the time — it’s EchoStar now — was going to be the fourth competitor. This was the rationale that they gave in terms of the approval of the transaction. Dish needed low-band spectrum. The problem is Ergen went about his business, he was trying to build a network, and then he just couldn

item.title: Neto double gives Chelsea win; marred by Martinez injury
item.description: Pedro Neto’s double condemned Everton to a first defeat of the season as Chelsea won 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite the loss of goalkeeper Emi Martinez to a head injury. Neto opened the scoring inside the first minute of the second half and secured the three points during the 11 added minutes following the lengthy treatment given to the stricken Martinez. The Argentine international was involved in a sickening head clash with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital. Victory lifts Chelsea above the Toffees into the top four of the Premier League. After a slow start, a fiery-tempered encounter sparked into life when Everton midfielder Harrison Armstrong launched into a tackle on Josh Acheampong for the first of five first-half yellow cards. That challenge also enlivened the home crowd and spurred Everton on to their best spell of the game. Thierno Barry was guilty of another wasteful day in front of goal as the Frenchman planted a header from Jack Grealish’s cross too close to Martinez. Chelsea have made a habit of fast starts under Xabi Alonso, but it took until four minutes before half-time to threaten when Moises Caicedo blasted off the bar from a well-worked corner. Everton were furious that Morgan Rogers escaped a second booking just before the break after a thunderous clash with England team-mate James Garner. That proved to be a huge decision as the visitors this time flew out of the blocks at the start of the second period. Jorrel Hato got to the byline and his low cross fell to Neto, who had time to control before firing low past Pickford. Chelsea had not kept a Premier League clean sheet in 22 matches stretching back to January, but were rarely troubled by an Everton side short on forward options despite the loss of Martinez. The treatment for the goalkeeper threatened to halt Chelsea’s momentum as they controlled the second half. Belgian Mike Penders replaced Martinez for his first Premier League appearance but had little to do bar dealing with a few desperate Everton crosses. At the other end Pickford made a fine save to deny Joao Pedro. But Chelsea did get their second goal when Neto coolly stroked into the bottom corner after Jordan Henderson’s free-kick was blocked by the Everton wall. The post Neto double gives Chelsea win; marred by Martinez injury appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Neto double at Everton leads Chelsea to victory marred by Martínez head injury
item.description: Chelsea have returned from the international break with a spirit, authority and resilience that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. Their troubles at Everton, not a happy hunting ground in recent years, were confined to the seven minutes Emi Martínez needed treatment for a head injury as Pedro Neto’s double delivered a deserved victory in the Merseyside sunshine. The Argentina goalkeeper was taken to hospital for tests after an accidental collision with Jarrad Branthwaite left him with suspected concussion. “When he left the stadium he was conscious,” Alonso said. “Hopefully it is not too bad but we need to wait.” A first Premier League clean sheet since January, and a second successive win since losing at Brentford before the Nations League break, were otherwise secured with a minimum of fuss in a commanding second-half performance. Continue reading...

item.title: I’d Have Left Real Madrid If I Were Vinicius — Mourinho
item.description: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said on Saturday that if he were winger Vinicius Junior, he would have left the club this summer. The Brazilian was sent off during Madrid’s win over Villarreal last weekend for hair pulling and was banned for four matches, meaning he will miss the Clasico clash against Barcelona on October 25. Real Madrid’s Brazilian forward Vinicius Junior. Photo by Alvaro Medranda/Getty Images Vinicius, 26, has also been targeted regularly by opposition fans and been racially abused on many occasions since joining Madrid in 2018. “He’s a spectacular kid who it’s easy to have a good relationship with,” Mourinho told reporters. “He’s a fantastic boy, tremendous credit to him for the fact that he keeps living and surviving and still having a smile… “If it were me in his place, probably I wouldn’t be here. In this last summer I would have forced an exit to a league, a country, to somewhere there are rival clubs and stadiums that respect him.” In the summer, Vinicius signed a new contract with Real Madrid until 2032. Question marks remain over whether Madrid can line up with attacking superstars Vinicius, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham together, without losing balance. “Because he loves Real Madrid, for loving the club and the city, for believing that things can always improve, he renewed, and he keeps on smiling,” continued Mourinho. “No one or nobody can… well, influence him negatively, yes, because he’s human… but take away his joy of living and working and being with his teammates, no, no one can do that.” Mourinho took Vinicius off during the 4-3 Champions League win at Roma on Wednesday, with the winger still struggling to return to the form that helped him win the competition twice under Carlo Ancelotti. Mourinho said he was happy that Vinicius’s ban was four matches, saying he thought some hidden figures at the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee “would give him one or two more”. ‘There Are Limits’ Madrid face Sevilla on Sunday, aiming not to fall further behind league leaders Barcelona, who visit Real Betis later on Saturday. Hansi Flick’s Barcelona have won every single match this season and are six points ahead of fourth-placed Real Madrid. Los Blancos and Mourinho have blamed referees for some of their results, including the 2-1 derby defeat by Atletico Madrid in September. On Friday, Real Madrid called for La Liga president Javier Tebas to resign after he compared the club’s efforts to discredit referees to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels. Tebas later attempted to clarify that he was drawing comparisons with “those propaganda techniques” and not with the ideology of the Nazis. “I don’t want to talk about this, there are limits, and there are limits. You can only excuse it if it’s a clinical case — otherwise there’s no excuse,” said Mourinho. “I don’t want to go down that road. item.title: FG destroys over 19,000 illicit weapons in anti-terrorism drive — Ribadu
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki The Federal Government has disclosed that it has destroyed more than 19,000 illicit weapons since 2022 as part of sustained efforts to dismantle the operational capacity of terrorists, bandits and other criminal networks threatening Nigeria’s security. The National Security Adviser (NSA), Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, disclosed this on Saturday in Sokoto during a high-level brainstorming session on tackling banditry in Sokoto State, stressing that the government was intensifying efforts to stem the proliferation of illegal firearms and restore lasting peace to vulnerable communities. The dialogue, themed “Coping with Banditry in Sokoto State: A Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue for Prevention, Containment and Community Resilience,” was convened by the Sokoto Advancement Forum (SAF) in collaboration with the Centre for Peace Studies, Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto. It brought security concerns, community resilience and coordinated action to the forefront of discussions on addressing insecurity in the North-West. Ribadu, who was represented by Barrister Zakariyya Mijinyawa, said the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was strengthening the national security architecture through intensified military operations, intelligence gathering, law enforcement, border surveillance and improved inter-agency collaboration. He maintained that defeating banditry required a coordinated strategy capable of dismantling criminal networks, disrupting their supply chains and preventing armed groups from exploiting security gaps. He identified Operation FANSAN YAMMA as a critical platform for coordinating security operations across the North-West, noting that sustained pressure on criminal elements remained necessary to protect lives, secure communities and prevent armed groups from establishing safe havens. He said the government would continue to reinforce operational cooperation among security agencies to confront emerging threats across the region. Highlighting recent weapons-control operations, the NSA cited figures from the National Centre for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons (NCCSALW), whose Director-General, retired Deputy Inspector-General of Police Johnson Kokumo, was identified in his remarks. According to Ribadu, the centre recovered 5,449 firearms and destroyed 1,419 illicit weapons during nationwide operations in September 2026, underscoring the continuing challenge posed by illegal arms trafficking. “These figures demonstrate the importance of sustained weapons-control operations. The NCCSALW and relevant security agencies will continue to strengthen efforts to disrupt arms-trafficking networks, trace recovered weapons and prevent illicit firearms from reaching criminal groups,” he said. Ribadu, however, cautioned that military action and weapons seizures alone would not deliver sustainable peace unless accompanied by effective governance and a sustained government presence in communities recovered from criminal groups. item.dc:creator: Henry Oduah
item.content:encoded: By Musa Ubandawaki The Federal Government has disclosed that it has destroyed more than 19,000 illicit weapons since 2022 as part of sustained efforts to dismantle the operational capacity of terrorists, bandits and other criminal networks threatening Nigeria’s security. The National Security Adviser (NSA), Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, disclosed this on Saturday in Sokoto during a high-level brainstorming session on tackling banditry in Sokoto State, stressing that the government was intensifying efforts to stem the proliferation of illegal firearms and restore lasting peace to vulnerable communities. The dialogue, themed “Coping with Banditry in Sokoto State: A Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue for Prevention, Containment and Community Resilience,” was convened by the Sokoto Advancement Forum (SAF) in collaboration with the Centre for Peace Studies, Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto. It brought security concerns, community resilience and coordinated action to the forefront of discussions on addressing insecurity in the North-West. Ribadu, who was represented by Barrister Zakariyya Mijinyawa, said the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was strengthening the national security architecture through intensified military operations, intelligence gathering, law enforcement, border surveillance and improved inter-agency collaboration. He maintained that defeating banditry required a coordinated strategy capable of dismantling criminal networks, disrupting their supply chains and preventing armed groups from exploiting security gaps. He identified Operation FANSAN YAMMA as a critical platform for coordinating security operations across the North-West, noting that sustained pressure on criminal elements remained necessary to protect lives, secure communities and prevent armed groups from establishing safe havens. He said the government would continue to reinforce operational cooperation among security agencies to confront emerging threats across the region. Highlighting recent weapons-control operations, the NSA cited figures from the National Centre for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons (NCCSALW), whose Director-General, retired Deputy Inspector-General of Police Johnson Kokumo, was identified in his remarks. According to Ribadu, the centre recovered 5,449 firearms and destroyed 1,419 illicit weapons during nationwide operations in September 2026, underscoring the continuing challenge posed by illegal arms trafficking. “These figures demonstrate the importance of sustained weapons-control operations. The NCCSALW and relevant security agencies will continue to strengthen efforts to disrupt arms-trafficking networks, trace recovered weapons and prevent illicit firearms from reaching criminal groups,” he said. Ribadu, however, cautioned that military action and weapons seizures alone would not deliver sustainable peace unless accompanied by effective governance and a sustained government presence in communities recovered from criminal groups. He argued that security operations must be backed by measures that restore public confidence, rebuild local institutions and enable displaced and vulnerable populations to resume their normal lives without the constant threat of violence. To strengthen coordination, he said the Office of the National Security Adviser was advancing a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach through the National Crisis Management Doctrine (NCMD). The framework, he explained, was designed to improve preparedness, strengthen collaboration among relevant institutions and ensure that security responses were coordinated rather than fragmented across government agencies and community structures. Addressing the peculiar security challenges confronting Sokoto State, Ribadu called for intelligence-led operations to deny bandits access to safe havens around vulnerable settlements, forest corridors and border communities. He stressed the importance of supporting State Forest Guards and NSCDC Agro-Rangers as part of broader efforts to improve surveillance, protect rural populations and disrupt the movement of criminal groups. He also underscored the need for stronger cross-border intelligence-sharing and functional early-warning mechanisms linking local authorities, traditional rulers, community leaders and security focal points. According to him, timely reporting and rapid responses to credible security alerts would be crucial to preventing attacks and protecting residents in vulnerable areas, including Sabon Birni, Isa, Tangaza and Goronyo. The NSA further called for stronger community participation in the fight against banditry, warning that misinformation, economic hardship and the vulnerability of young people could undermine security interventions if left unaddressed. He urged stakeholders to protect livelihoods, expand access to education and employment opportunities, and develop community-based measures capable of discouraging youth recruitment into criminal networks. “Reintegration must never replace justice or reward violence. National security frameworks can succeed only when communities help translate them into local action,” Ribadu declared, emphasising that reconciliation and rehabilitation efforts must operate within the framework of accountability and the rule of law. His position highlighted the need to balance opportunities for peace with justice for victims and measures to prevent the recurrence of violence. He commended the Sokoto Advancement Forum (SAF) for developing its Blueprint for the Strategic Development of Sokoto State, urging participants to translate the dialogue into measurable actions rather than allowing the discussions to end as another policy exercise without practical consequences. He specifically called for the development of a community security and early-warning plan that would establish clear responsibilities, improve information-sharing and strengthen cooperation between residents and security agencies. “Let this dialogue mark a decisive step towards a safer Sokoto where communities live without fear, agriculture and commerce flourish, young people pursue productive lives, and public institutions protect every citizen,” Ribadu said. He maintained that restoring security in Sokoto and the wider North-West would require sustained commitment, collective responsibility and a comprehensive strategy that combines military pressure, intelligence-driven policing, effective governance, economic opportunity and community resilience. item.title: The Best Transformers Movie That No One Watched Finds New Life on Streaming
item.description: Under director Michael Bay, Paramount built a billion-dollar franchise across five live-action Transformers movies . But after Bay's final turn behind the camera, 2017's Transformers: The Last Knight , the robots-in-disguise franchise started to go in unpredictable new directions. The 2018 prequel Bumblebee was, unlike Bay's films, a critical and commercial hit, though it didn't hit the billion-dollar highs of earlier films. 2023's Transformers: Rise of the Beasts failed to turn the franchise around the way Paramount hoped.

item.title: Ex-Senegal president Macky Sall withdraws as candidate for UN leader
item.description: Former president of Senegal Macky Sall on Saturday withdrew from the seven-person race to be the next UN secretary-general, a day after an informal UN Security Council poll produced no clear favourite. In a statement released on social media, Sall said he had noted the result of the poll and “hoped to contribute now the emergence of a consensus candidate within the Security Council”. He added that “the results of different test votes indicate a choice favouring a candidate — perhaps female –from the Latin America-Caribbean region.” A UN diplomat said Friday that all seven hopefuls had received a vote of “discourage,” effectively a veto, from a permanent UN Security Council member in anonymous informal polling. Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan — who has been among the frontrunners in five previous polls — received the most “encourage” votes, but also got five “discourage” votes, including two from permanent members of the 15-country council. US media reports suggest Washington opposes all seven contenders. Among those considered by diplomats to be potential entrants are Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza under the US-backed “Board of Peace,” and the UAE’s minister of state for foreign affairs Lana Nusseibeh. Turkey’s Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu, secretary general of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), has also had his name floated. The other candidates are Guyanese ex-foreign minister Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, Argentina’s Rafael Grossi, who heads the UN nuclear watchdog, Ecuador’s Ivonne A-Baki and Maria Fernanda Espinosa and Uganda’s Olara Otunnu. The outgoing secretary-general, Antonio Guterres of Portugal, ends his second five-year term on December 31. Even if a candidate earns the required nine votes from the 15 in the Security Council, they must also avoid a veto by the five major powers, which are deeply divided. item.title: 2027: We’ll defeat Tinubu in 12 states – Makinde’s campaign
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, MDPCO, has vowed that its candidate, Seyi Makinde of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, will defeat President Bola Tinubu in the 12 battleground states identified by the President, including Rivers State and the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Abuja, in the January 2027 presidential election. The campaign organisation said Tinubu’s planned visits to the states would do little to change what it described as growing opposition to his re-election, blaming the hardship Nigerians face on his administration’s policies and accusing members of his inner circle of aggravating public resentment through political arrogance. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Hon. Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the MDPCO said Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA agenda was gaining traction across the country, particularly among young people, and challenged Tinubu to test his popularity through direct engagement with voters rather than campaign rallies. The organisation listed Oyo, Kaduna, Rivers, Plateau, Borno, Enugu, Bauchi, Sokoto, Delta, Kano, Adamawa and Lagos as the 12 states Tinubu had identified for personal campaign visits, claiming the move reflected concern over Makinde’s growing political foothold. “Mr. President should know that his visit to these states, if he eventually does, will not in any way change the direction or the determination of the people to vote him out,” the statement said. The campaign challenged Tinubu to travel by road through the states and see for himself the condition of federal highways, the living conditions of Nigerians and the state of public infrastructure. “We challenge President Tinubu not to have a change of mind but visit the states to face the people. He should travel around the country by road and witness the decrepit state of federal highways, the squalor in which Nigerians live and the level of infrastructural decay across the country,” it said. The MDPCO accused the administration of spending trillions of naira on wasteful programmes and projects while Nigerians grapple with economic hardship. It also dismissed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda as ineffective, arguing that Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA programme offered a more practical alternative. The proposed agenda, according to the organisation, centres on an inclusive, four-year transitional government of national unity, with education, the economy, security and socio-political reforms as its four priority areas. It said Makinde’s economic plan would tackle poverty through increased production, while his security strategy would combine intelligence gathering, social reorientation and kinetic and non-kinetic measures. The education component would expand access to quality, functional education, while institutional reforms would promote inclusive governance and responsible leadership. item.title: Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion — Makinde
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country. Makinde said Christians could not afford to stand aloof from politics on the grounds that it was dirty or that they should not serve under leaders who did not share their faith, stressing that national transformation required their active participation. He spoke on Saturday in Abuja after receiving a Christian Icon Award at the Christian Association of Nigeria’s (CAN) 50th anniversary celebration. The governor, who is the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), said Christians should draw lessons from biblical figures who accepted difficult assignments in pursuit of a greater purpose. “It is typical for us to say, ‘Politics is dirty. I don’t want to be yoked with unbelievers’, and things like that. But we must look at biblical examples,” he said. Makinde cited David, who, despite having been anointed king, served in the palace of Saul, from whom God had departed. He said the biblical account should challenge Christians who believe they cannot serve under leaders of different religious persuasions. “I will use this opportunity to encourage our Christian brothers and sisters across the country to rise up and participate in the agenda to transform Nigeria and reset our country,” he said. Makinde urged Christians to focus on the hardship confronting Nigerians rather than allowing religious differences to define their engagement with national affairs. “Our problem is not primarily a religious one. Our problem in this country is poverty — grinding poverty,” he said. “At this stage, we must focus on addressing the issues currently confronting us. Those are the challenges we need to tackle.” The post Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion — Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The 8 Best Vampire Books Not Written by Anne Rice
item.description: In vampire stories, the immortal creatures of the night often trace their lineage back centuries. The authors of these stories are themselves part of a creative bloodline that took myths about blood-sucking monsters and turned them into timeless stories of horror . The genre’s foundations were laid by Sheridan Le Fanu's 1872 novella Carmilla and Bram Stoker’s 1897 novel Dracula , but Anne Rice is the undisputed master of the modern vampire story.

item.title: Nigeria’s stability will attract long-term investment — Cardoso
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Olayemi Cardoso, has said sustained macroeconomic stability, declining inflation and confidence in policy direction will attract long-term investment into Nigeria, boosting production and creating jobs. Cardoso, who spoke alongside the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele at the 2026 IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings said Nigeria’s economic recovery was creating opportunities to deepen investor confidence and mobilise capital for productive activities. According to him, “The global economy has shown resilience in the face of fragmentation and significant headwinds, but the environment remains fragile. What is important for Nigeria is to sustain the progress we have made and create the conditions for private investment to flourish.” He said the CBN would continue to pursue policies aimed at restoring price stability, strengthening the foreign exchange market and improving the economy’s capacity to withstand external shocks. “We are focused on price stability. Our decisions are data-dependent, and we will continue to communicate clearly so that businesses, households and investors understand the direction of monetary policy,” Cardoso said. The governor stated that the decline in inflation provided an opportunity to recalibrate monetary policy while maintaining a sufficiently tight stance to consolidate the gains achieved. “Inflation has come down significantly from the levels we saw previously. Headline inflation was 14.63 per cent in September 2026, compared with about 34.8 per cent at the end of 2024. That is an important development, but we must ensure that the decline is sustained,” he said. He added that lower inflation would help businesses plan more effectively, improve investment decisions and support production and employment. “When inflation is high and unpredictable, businesses find it difficult to plan. It affects their costs, their pricing decisions and their willingness to invest. Our objective is to achieve price stability that supports sustainable growth and allows businesses to make longer-term decisions,” he said. Cardoso said the CBN’s medium-term objective remained the achievement of single-digit inflation, stressing that monetary policy would be guided by economic conditions rather than pressure to follow the decisions of other central banks. “We cannot simply copy what other central banks are doing. Our decisions must reflect Nigeria’s circumstances, the structure of our economy and the evidence before us. The objective is to make decisions that are appropriate for our economy while maintaining credibility,” he said. item.dc:creator: Henry Oduah
item.content:encoded: By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Olayemi Cardoso, has said sustained macroeconomic stability, declining inflation and confidence in policy direction will attract long-term investment into Nigeria, boosting production and creating jobs. Cardoso, who spoke alongside the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele at the 2026 IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings said Nigeria’s economic recovery was creating opportunities to deepen investor confidence and mobilise capital for productive activities. According to him, “The global economy has shown resilience in the face of fragmentation and significant headwinds, but the environment remains fragile. What is important for Nigeria is to sustain the progress we have made and create the conditions for private investment to flourish.” He said the CBN would continue to pursue policies aimed at restoring price stability, strengthening the foreign exchange market and improving the economy’s capacity to withstand external shocks. “We are focused on price stability. Our decisions are data-dependent, and we will continue to communicate clearly so that businesses, households and investors understand the direction of monetary policy,” Cardoso said. The governor stated that the decline in inflation provided an opportunity to recalibrate monetary policy while maintaining a sufficiently tight stance to consolidate the gains achieved. “Inflation has come down significantly from the levels we saw previously. Headline inflation was 14.63 per cent in September 2026, compared with about 34.8 per cent at the end of 2024. That is an important development, but we must ensure that the decline is sustained,” he said. He added that lower inflation would help businesses plan more effectively, improve investment decisions and support production and employment. “When inflation is high and unpredictable, businesses find it difficult to plan. It affects their costs, their pricing decisions and their willingness to invest. Our objective is to achieve price stability that supports sustainable growth and allows businesses to make longer-term decisions,” he said. Cardoso said the CBN’s medium-term objective remained the achievement of single-digit inflation, stressing that monetary policy would be guided by economic conditions rather than pressure to follow the decisions of other central banks. “We cannot simply copy what other central banks are doing. Our decisions must reflect Nigeria’s circumstances, the structure of our economy and the evidence before us. The objective is to make decisions that are appropriate for our economy while maintaining credibility,” he said. On foreign exchange, the governor said improved stability was strengthening confidence in the naira and providing a more predictable environment for investors. “Our external reserves are now above $55 billion, the highest level in 18 years. That gives us a stronger buffer against external shocks and helps to support confidence in the economy,” he said. He added that the CBN was working to strengthen formal diaspora remittances as part of efforts to diversify Nigeria’s foreign exchange earnings. “Formal remittances are approaching $1 billion monthly. We want to build on that progress because remittances are an important source of foreign exchange for Nigeria. We must continue to improve the channels through which these funds enter the formal financial system,” Cardoso said. The governor also highlighted the need to mobilise long-term domestic and foreign capital to finance infrastructure, businesses and other productive sectors. “We need to deepen our capital markets and create more opportunities for long-term investment. Stability is important because investors need confidence that the rules will remain predictable and that their investments can be managed within a credible policy environment,” he said. He said the CBN would strengthen collaboration with development finance institutions, including the Africa Finance Corporation, AFC, to support investment and economic development. “The role of the CBN is to maintain monetary and financial stability. Development finance institutions have their own mandates to support productive investment. We need to work together more closely so that stability can translate into financing for the real economy,” he said. Cardoso noted that the banking sector had also made progress through the recapitalisation exercise, which attracted substantial domestic investment. “Banks have raised about ₦4.65 trillion in fresh capital, and just over 70 per cent came from domestic investors. This is significant because it shows that Nigerian investors are willing to commit capital to the banking system,” he said. He said the stronger capital base would improve the resilience of the financial system, while emphasising the need for banks to remain well governed and capable of supporting economic activity. “Our task is to sustain confidence, maintain financial stability and ensure that the financial system remains strong enough to support the economy through changing conditions,” Cardoso said. He added that the ultimate objective was to ensure that macroeconomic stability translated into higher investment, stronger production and more employment opportunities for Nigerians. item.title: Investors bank on Tinubu’s re-election, continuity of reforms — Oyedele
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe Nigeria’s economic reforms have strengthened investor confidence, with financial markets and the international community pricing in the prospect of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and continuity of the policies beyond the 2027 general election, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said. Oyedele, who spoke during a press briefing alongside the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, at the 2026 IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, said investors were concerned about whether political developments would lead to a reversal of the government’s economic reforms. He said: “The markets and the international community have been pricing in the prospect of a second term for the President, and they expect continuity in the reforms.” Responding to questions about the forthcoming election and the implications for economic policy, the minister acknowledged that investors were seeking assurances that Nigeria would not abandon the reforms that had helped stabilise the economy. According to him, investors had raised questions about the possibility of political pressure forcing the government to reverse its policies. “They ask, ‘Are you under pressure because of elections?” Oyedele said, recounting the concerns investors had expressed. He maintained that the government’s reform programme was driven by the need to put the economy on a sustainable footing, rather than by political calculations. “It is not because I am trying to help Mr President win re-election,” he said, explaining the rationale for maintaining the policies. Oyedele said the government remained committed to sustaining the reforms, insisting that a reversal would undermine confidence, trigger capital flight and renew pressure on the naira. “There will be no return to fuel subsidies or multiple exchange rates,” he declared. He explained that the recent decision by NNPC Retail to offer a discount on petrol was a commercial decision and should not be interpreted as a return to government-funded fuel subsidies. “What you are seeing from NNPC Retail is a commercial decision. It is not a subsidy. A company can decide to reduce its margin or offer a discount as part of its business strategy. That does not mean the government has brought back subsidies,” he said. The minister warned that reversing the reforms would carry significant economic costs. “If you reverse these reforms, investors will respond. Capital will leave, pressure will return to the foreign exchange market and the naira will come under pressure. We cannot afford to go back to where we were,” he said. item.dc:creator: Henry Oduah
item.content:encoded: By Babajide Komolafe Nigeria’s economic reforms have strengthened investor confidence, with financial markets and the international community pricing in the prospect of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and continuity of the policies beyond the 2027 general election, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said. Oyedele, who spoke during a press briefing alongside the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, at the 2026 IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, said investors were concerned about whether political developments would lead to a reversal of the government’s economic reforms. He said: “The markets and the international community have been pricing in the prospect of a second term for the President, and they expect continuity in the reforms.” Responding to questions about the forthcoming election and the implications for economic policy, the minister acknowledged that investors were seeking assurances that Nigeria would not abandon the reforms that had helped stabilise the economy. According to him, investors had raised questions about the possibility of political pressure forcing the government to reverse its policies. “They ask, ‘Are you under pressure because of elections?” Oyedele said, recounting the concerns investors had expressed. He maintained that the government’s reform programme was driven by the need to put the economy on a sustainable footing, rather than by political calculations. “It is not because I am trying to help Mr President win re-election,” he said, explaining the rationale for maintaining the policies. Oyedele said the government remained committed to sustaining the reforms, insisting that a reversal would undermine confidence, trigger capital flight and renew pressure on the naira. “There will be no return to fuel subsidies or multiple exchange rates,” he declared. He explained that the recent decision by NNPC Retail to offer a discount on petrol was a commercial decision and should not be interpreted as a return to government-funded fuel subsidies. “What you are seeing from NNPC Retail is a commercial decision. It is not a subsidy. A company can decide to reduce its margin or offer a discount as part of its business strategy. That does not mean the government has brought back subsidies,” he said. The minister warned that reversing the reforms would carry significant economic costs. “If you reverse these reforms, investors will respond. Capital will leave, pressure will return to the foreign exchange market and the naira will come under pressure. We cannot afford to go back to where we were,” he said. Economic Growth Oyedele also expressed confidence that Nigeria would outperform the economic growth projections of the International Monetary Fund, IMF, and the World Bank, arguing that the government’s ambition should not be limited to the forecasts of multilateral institutions. “The IMF and the World Bank make projections based on the information and assumptions available to them. We respect their work, but our ambition cannot be limited to their projections,” he said. “We are targeting growth of seven per cent. That is what we believe Nigeria needs to create jobs, improve incomes and reduce poverty. We must be ambitious, but we must also do the work required to achieve that growth.” He identified food, energy and logistics costs as major constraints on economic expansion, saying reforms in these areas would be critical to reducing inflation and stimulating investment. “If we want stronger growth, we have to address the things that make production expensive in Nigeria. Food, energy and logistics are major pressure points. We need to bring down those costs and improve the efficiency of doing business,” he said. On inflation, Oyedele said the government wanted a sustained decline that would create room for lower interest rates and improve access to credit for businesses. “We want inflation to come down to low single digits. When inflation is high, interest rates are also high, and businesses struggle to borrow at a cost that allows them to make a profit. Our objective is to create an environment where businesses can invest and grow,” he said. The minister disclosed that Nigeria had presented 65 investment projects valued at $78.5 billion to prospective investors, covering energy, transportation, industry, mining, agriculture, healthcare and urban services. He said attracting private capital into the projects would support economic expansion and employment creation. Oyedele stressed that the ultimate test of the reforms would be their impact on ordinary Nigerians. “Stability is earned, and growth is a task. It is not enough to say that the numbers are improving. We must ensure that growth creates jobs, that businesses are able to expand and that Nigerians can see the benefits in their daily lives,” he said. He urged Nigerians to recognise the opportunities emerging from the reforms, adding that policy consistency would be critical to sustaining investor confidence and achieving stronger economic growth. item.title: COAS Shuaibu Arrives In Borno After Tinubu Ordered Rescue Of All Abductees
item.description: The Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shuaibu, arrived in Maiduguri, the Borno State capital, on Saturday, following directives from President Bola Tinubu to rescue all abducted persons nationwide. Shuaibu arrived in the state capital at about 11 am on Saturday. On October 15, the Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, said Tinubu gave the directive to heads of security agencies during a security meeting presided over by the President at the Presidential Villa, Abuja. Tinubu had also ordered that no terrorist or bandit camp remained anywhere in Nigeria. Musa said Tinubu also directed the service chiefs and other security heads to guarantee a safe environment for Nigerians to vote in the elections scheduled for January. “The directive from the President is: all of us must go all out to fish out and rescue all those that have been abducted, kidnapped, wherever they are. “There shouldn’t be any camp of any terrorists or bandits anywhere in Nigeria,” he said. The post COAS Shuaibu Arrives In Borno After Tinubu Ordered Rescue Of All Abductees appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Police rescue baby allegedly sold by mother for N2m
item.description: The Police Command in Oyo State has rescued a one-month-old baby girl, allegedly sold by her mother for N2 million to one Folawewo in Ido Local Government Area of Ibadan. The Police Publicity Relations Officer (PPRO), DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, made this known in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday in Ibadan. Ayanlade alleged that the health facility owner facilitated the sale of the baby girl after her mother delivered there. The PPRO said that a woman, Mary Amos, reported the incident to the police on Thursday, at about 6.00 p.m. The complainant, said the police spokesperson, claimed that her 23-year-old daughter gave birth to a baby girl on Sept. 6 at Ebepraise Health Centre, Ido. “She further reported that her daughter disappeared with the baby about seven days after delivery and could not provide a satisfactory account of the child’s whereabouts, raising suspicions that the baby might have been sold. “Acting on the report, police operatives arrested the baby’s mother for questioning. “She confessed during interrogation that the owner of the health facility and one Oludunni lured her into the arrangement and facilitated the sale of the baby to one Folawewo,” he said. Ayanlade said investigations later revealed that the baby’s mother received N1 million of the N2 million, while the health facility owner and Oludunni received N500,000 each. According to him, the one-month-old baby girl has been rescued, and efforts are currently ongoing to arrest the buyer of the baby, Folawemo, and all other persons involved to face justice. He reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting children and other vulnerable persons. He also urged members of the public to promptly report any suspected cases of child trafficking and related offences. (NAN) The post Police rescue baby allegedly sold by mother for N2m appeared first on Vanguard News .
